titulo.es: Abrir sesiones contra la base de metadatos de Airflow desde el código de las tareas
titulo.en: Opening sessions on the Airflow metadata database from task code

porque.es: En Airflow 2 el código de usuario podía importar sesiones y tocar la base de metadatos: un riesgo de seguridad y demasiadas conexiones. Airflow 3.0 (abril de 2025) lo impide en las tareas: el estado de los DAG, el historial y las ejecuciones se consultan por la API REST o el contexto, y la guía de migración recomienda el cliente Python de Airflow. El código del autor aún puede tener acceso directo en el procesador de DAG y el triggerer.
porque.en: In Airflow 2 user code could import sessions and touch the metadata database: a security risk and too many connections. Airflow 3.0 (April 2025) blocks it in tasks: DAG state, history and runs are queried through the REST API or the context, and the migration guide recommends the Airflow Python client. Author code may still have direct access in the DAG File Processor and the Triggerer.

evidencia.cita: Task code can no longer directly access the metadata database. Interactions with DAG state, task history, or DAG runs must be performed via the Airflow REST API or exposed context.
User code could import sessions and perform malicious actions on the Airflow metadata database. The number of connections to the database was excessive, leading to scaling challenges.
Note that Dag author code potentially still executes with direct database access in the Dag File Processor and Triggerer

nota.es: Airflow 3.0 impide el acceso directo a la base de metadatos desde las tareas; la guía de migración explica el riesgo que tenía en Airflow 2.
nota.en: Airflow 3.0 blocks direct metadata database access from tasks; the migration guide explains the risk it carried in Airflow 2.

porque.es: En MySQL, utf8 es un alias de utf8mb3, que no guarda caracteres de 4 bytes como los emojis. utf8mb3 está deprecado. Ojo: las notas de MySQL 8.0 GA (2018) anunciaron que utf8 pasaría a significar utf8mb4, pero no ha ocurrido; desde la 9.5 solo existe un modo SQL, desactivado por defecto, que lo cambia (y la 8.4 LTS no lo tiene).
porque.en: In MySQL, utf8 is an alias for utf8mb3, which cannot store 4-byte characters such as emoji. utf8mb3 is deprecated. Note: the MySQL 8.0 GA notes (2018) announced utf8 would come to mean utf8mb4, but it has not happened; since 9.5 there is only an SQL mode, off by default, that changes it (and 8.4 LTS lacks it).

evidencia.titulo: What's New in MySQL 8.0? (Generally Available) (MySQL blog)

The mode is disabled by default, preserving the previous utf8mb3 interpretation.

titulo.es: Combinar el feedback explícito con señales implícitas (reintentos, reformulaciones, abandonos) detectadas en las trazas
titulo.en: Combining explicit feedback with implicit signals (retries, rephrasings, abandonment) detected in traces

porque.es: Las señales implícitas están en cada traza (el usuario reintenta, reformula o edita el borrador) sin pedirle nada, aunque hay que interpretarlas. Junto con los votos, la revisión de transcripts y las evals dan la imagen completa que pide Anthropic. El voto solo, como señal principal, es un antipatrón (ver pulgar-arriba-abajo-como-senal-principal-de-calidad).
porque.en: Implicit signals are in every trace (the user retries, rephrases or edits the draft) without asking anything, though they need interpretation. Together with votes, transcript review and evals they give the complete picture Anthropic asks for. Votes alone, as the main signal, are an anti-pattern (see pulgar-arriba-abajo-como-senal-principal-de-calidad).

titulo.es: Comprobar la licencia de la versión concreta de Redis o Elasticsearch antes de actualizar
titulo.en: Checking the licence of the specific Redis or Elasticsearch version before upgrading

porque.es: Ambos cambiaron de licencia al subir de versión: Elasticsearch 7.11 (febrero de 2021) dejó Apache 2.0 por SSPL/Elastic License y Redis 7.4 (anunciado el 20 de marzo de 2024) dejó BSD por RSALv2/SSPLv1. Después los dos añadieron la AGPLv3, aprobada por la OSI: Elasticsearch en 8.16 (noviembre de 2024) y Redis en Redis 8 (mayo de 2025). Hoy vuelven a ofrecer una licencia de código abierto, así que pasarse a un fork ya no es la única vía para eso; quien necesite una licencia permisiva tiene los forks Valkey (BSD) y OpenSearch (Apache 2.0) (ver redis-con-licencia-bsd y elasticsearch-con-licencia-apache-2).
porque.en: Both changed licence on a version upgrade: Elasticsearch 7.11 (February 2021) moved from Apache 2.0 to SSPL/Elastic License and Redis 7.4 (announced on 20 March 2024) moved from BSD to RSALv2/SSPLv1. Later both added the OSI-approved AGPLv3: Elasticsearch in 8.16 (November 2024) and Redis in Redis 8 (May 2025). Today they offer an open source licence again, so moving to a fork is no longer the only way to get one; those who need a permissive licence have the Valkey (BSD) and OpenSearch (Apache 2.0) forks (see redis-con-licencia-bsd and elasticsearch-con-licencia-apache-2).

evidencia.cita: The default throughout the repository is a dual license under the Server Side Public License, v 1 and the Elastic License 2.0, unless the header specifies another license.
Consequently, Redis will no longer be distributed under the three-clause Berkeley Software Distribution (BSD).
The tl;dr is that we will be adding AGPL as another license option next to ELv2 and SSPL in the coming weeks.
The default throughout the repository is a triple license under the "GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 only", "the Server Side Public License, v 1", and the "Elastic License 2.0"

It’s all Apache 2.0. There’s no Contributor License Agreement.

titulo.es: Recorrer una lista de entidades y cargar sus relaciones una a una (consultas N+1)
titulo.en: Iterating over a list of entities and loading their relations one by one (N+1 queries)

porque.es: Recorrer N registros y cargar la relación de cada uno lanza N consultas extra. Rails (includes), Django (select_related, prefetch_related) e Hibernate (join fetch) documentan cómo cargarlo de una vez. En Spring, open-in-view puede esconder estas consultas en la vista (ver dejar-open-in-view-activado-por-defecto).
porque.en: Iterating N records and loading each one's relation fires N extra queries. Rails (includes), Django (select_related, prefetch_related) and Hibernate (join fetch) document how to load it in one go. In Spring, open-in-view can hide these queries in the view (see dejar-open-in-view-activado-por-defecto).

evidencia.titulo: Rails Guides — Active Record Query Interface: N + 1 Queries Problem
evidencia.cita: Retrieving a list of records N (where N is a number greater that 1) in a single query can sometimes trigger N extra queries; one for each record.
This is particularly important if you have a query that is executed in a loop, and could therefore end up doing many database queries, when only one is needed.
we need a way to request that an association be _eagerly_ fetched using a database `join`, thus protecting ourselves from the infamous N+1 selects.
Select fetching (the default) is extremely vulnerable to N+1 selects problems

nota.es: La referencia de Hibernate 3.3.2 (junio de 2009) ya avisa de que la carga por select por defecto es muy vulnerable al problema N+1 (es la fuente con fecha más antigua que tenemos, no el origen del problema); Rails y Django lo documentan hoy con sus soluciones.
nota.en: The Hibernate 3.3.2 reference (June 2009) already warns that default select fetching is extremely vulnerable to N+1 (the oldest dated source we have, not the origin of the problem); Rails and Django document it today with their fixes.

evidencia.cita: Whether a copy or a reference is returned for a setting operation, may depend on the context. This is sometimes called chained assignment and should be avoided.

titulo.es: Añadir una columna con DEFAULT en PostgreSQL en varios pasos (nullable, rellenar por lotes, fijar el default) para evitar reescribir la tabla

porque.es: Hasta PostgreSQL 10, ADD COLUMN con DEFAULT reescribía la tabla entera y sus índices. Desde PostgreSQL 11 (octubre de 2018) un DEFAULT no volátil se guarda en los metadatos y el ALTER es muy rápido incluso en tablas grandes; un DEFAULT volátil (p. ej. clock_timestamp()) sigue reescribiendo.
porque.en: Up to PostgreSQL 10, ADD COLUMN with a DEFAULT rewrote the whole table and its indexes. Since PostgreSQL 11 (October 2018) a non-volatile DEFAULT is stored in the metadata and the ALTER is very fast even on large tables; a volatile DEFAULT (e.g. clock_timestamp()) still rewrites.

cuando.es: PostgreSQL 11 o posterior con un DEFAULT no volátil (una constante)
cuando.en: PostgreSQL 11 or later with a non-volatile DEFAULT (a constant)

porque.es: El valor se guarda en los metadatos y no se reescribe la tabla.
porque.en: The value is stored in the metadata and the table is not rewritten.

cuando.es: DEFAULT volátil (clock_timestamp(), etc.), o PostgreSQL 10 o anterior
cuando.en: a volatile DEFAULT (clock_timestamp(), etc.), or PostgreSQL 10 or earlier

porque.es: Sigue reescribiéndose la tabla entera y sus índices.

porque.en: A plain CREATE INDEX blocks writes to the table until it finishes, and indexing a very large table can take hours. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (PostgreSQL 8.2, December 2006) builds it without blocking writes, at the cost of scanning the table twice and taking longer.

porque.en: Redis 7.2 and earlier are BSD. Since 7.4 (change announced on 20 March 2024) it is RSALv2/SSPLv1, and since Redis 8 (May 2025) also AGPLv3, which is OSI-approved. This project was forked from the open source Redis project right before the transition to their new source available licenses.
Redis Open Source 7.2 and prior releases remain subject to the BSDv3 clause license
Consequently, Redis will no longer be distributed under the three-clause Berkeley Software Distribution (BSD).

porque.en: A single FLUSHALL from an attacker wipes all data. Since Redis 3.2 (May 2016) protected mode rejects outside connections when there is no password, and since Redis 6 (April 2020) there are ACLs with users.

evidencia.cita: Access to the Redis port should be denied to everybody but trusted clients in the network

The recommended authentication method, introduced in Redis 6, is via Access Control Lists

porque.es: KEYS es O(N) sobre todas las claves y puede hundir el rendimiento con bases grandes. La documentación de Redis dice que no se use en el código normal de la aplicación y propone SCAN (Redis 2.8, noviembre de 2013), que itera por partes.
porque.en: KEYS is O(N) over every key and can ruin performance on large databases. The Redis docs say not to use it in regular application code and suggest SCAN (Redis 2.8, November 2013), which iterates incrementally.

evidencia.cita: Don't use `KEYS` in your regular application code.

porque.es: Desde PostgreSQL 10 (2017) existen las columnas identity, que son estándar SQL. serial complica la gestión de esquemas, dependencias y permisos; la wiki de PostgreSQL solo lo admite para versiones anteriores a la 10 y casos raros (herencia de tablas, una secuencia compartida).
porque.en: Since PostgreSQL 10 (2017) there are identity columns, which are standard SQL. serial makes schema, dependency and permission management cumbersome; the PostgreSQL wiki only accepts it for versions before 10 and rare cases (table inheritance, a shared sequence).

evidencia.cita: These are similar to SERIAL columns, but are SQL standard compliant.

evidencia.cita: For new applications, identity columns should be used instead.
The serial types have some weird behaviors that make schema, dependency, and permission management unnecessarily cumbersome.

The data types serial and bigserial are not true types, but merely a notational convenience for setting up unique identifier columns (similar to the AUTO_INCREMENT property supported by some other databases).

porque.es: timestamp guarda «la foto de un reloj», no un momento: sin zona, el mismo valor significa cosas distintas según dónde se lea. La wiki de PostgreSQL lo desaconseja desde 2018, también para guardar horas UTC; lo admite si las fechas solo se guardan y se leen desde la aplicación, sin aritmética con ellas.
porque.en: timestamp stores "a picture of a clock", not a moment: without a zone, the same value means different things depending on where it is read. The PostgreSQL wiki has advised against it since 2018, also for storing UTC times; it accepts it if dates are only saved and read back by the app, with no arithmetic on them.

titulo.es: Usar UUIDv4 aleatorios como clave primaria indexada
titulo.en: Using random UUIDv4 values as an indexed primary key

porque.es: Los valores aleatorios caen en sitios dispersos del índice: el RFC 9562 (2024) dice que la diferencia frente a valores ordenados en el tiempo puede ser de un orden de magnitud o más. Pero el mismo RFC pide UUIDv4 cuando el identificador interviene en cualquier operación de seguridad, porque UUIDv7 revela cuándo se creó.
porque.en: Random values land scattered across the index: RFC 9562 (2024) says the difference versus time-ordered values can be one order of magnitude or more. But the same RFC asks for UUIDv4 when the identifier is used in any security operation, since UUIDv7 reveals when it was created.

cuando.es: clave interna indexada con muchas inserciones
cuando.en: internal indexed key with many inserts

porque.es: Ver uuidv7-como-clave-primaria.
porque.en: See uuidv7-como-clave-primaria.

cuando.es: el identificador se expone, interviene en algo de seguridad o no debe revelar cuándo se creó
cuando.en: the identifier is exposed, used in anything security-related, or must not reveal when it was created

evidencia.cita: UUID versions that are not time ordered, such as UUIDv4 (described in Section 5.4), have poor database-index locality.
The real-world differences in this approach of index locality versus random data inserts can be one order of magnitude or more.
Add UUID version 7 generation function uuidv7()
If UUIDs are required for use with any security operation within an application context in any shape or form, then UUIDv4 (Section 5.4) SHOULD be utilized.

nota.es: El RFC 9562 define UUIDv7, ordenado en el tiempo, y explica la mala localidad de UUIDv4 en índices.
nota.en: RFC 9562 defines time-ordered UUIDv7 and explains UUIDv4’s poor index locality.

titulo.es: Usar UUIDv7 (ordenados en el tiempo) como clave primaria cuando se necesita un UUID

porque.es: Los valores nuevos quedan juntos en el índice, como un autoincremento, pero siguen siendo UUID. PostgreSQL 18 los genera de serie. Si el identificador interviene en seguridad o no debe revelar cuándo se creó, el RFC pide UUIDv4.
porque.en: New values land together in the index, like an auto-increment, while still being UUIDs. PostgreSQL 18 generates them out of the box. If the identifier is security-related or must not reveal its creation time, the RFC asks for UUIDv4.

evidencia.cita: Time-ordered monotonic UUIDs benefit from greater database-index locality because the new values are near each other in the index.
the database-friendly uuidv7() function that provides better indexing and read performance for UUIDs.

Stack traces are harder to understand with ZoneJS.
By default, all asynchronous operations are inside the Angular zone, which triggers change detection automatically.

GitLab no la cuenta. Para el resto del código sigue valiendo la revisión humana (ver revision-de-ia-como-complemento-de-la-humana).
porque.en: Since 1 September 2026 GitHub lets (in preview, off by default) a Copilot approval satisfy the approval rule, restricted to PRs whose files match some paths and dismissed on new commits. GitLab does not count it. For the rest of the code, human review still applies (ver revision-de-ia-como-complemento-de-la-humana).

titulo.es: Compilar C++ de producción con la biblioteca estándar endurecida (-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS o _LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE)
titulo.en: Building production C++ with a hardened standard library (-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS or _LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE)

porque.es: Convierte accesos fuera de rango y otras violaciones de precondiciones en un fallo controlado en vez de comportamiento indefinido. OpenSSF lo incluye desde 2023 en sus opciones recomendadas, GCC 14 lo mete en -fhardened, libc++ recomienda su modo «fast» para la mayoría de proyectos, y el borrador de C++26 lo recoge como «implementación endurecida».
porque.en: It turns out-of-bounds access and other precondition violations into a controlled failure instead of undefined behaviour. OpenSSF has included it in its recommended options since 2023, GCC 14 puts it in -fhardened, libc++ recommends its "fast" mode for most projects, and the C++26 draft adopts it as a "hardened implementation".

porque.es: Cada cambio en un fichero grande hace crecer el repositorio y, con el tiempo, ralentiza `clone`, `fetch` y `pull`. GitHub bloquea ficheros de más de 100 MiB y recomienda repos de menos de 1 GB; Git LFS (anunciado en abril de 2015) deja en Git solo un puntero de texto y guarda el contenido fuera.
porque.en: Every change to a large file grows the repository and, over time, slows down `clone`, `fetch` and `pull`. GitHub blocks files over 100 MiB and recommends repos under 1 GB; Git LFS (announced April 2015) keeps only a text pointer in Git and stores the content elsewhere.

evidencia.cita: Git LFS is a new, open source extension that replaces large files with text pointers inside Git, while storing the file contents on a remote server like GitHub.

titulo.es: Serializar o deserializar datos con BinaryFormatter
titulo.en: Serializing or deserializing data with BinaryFormatter

porque.es: Deserializar con BinaryFormatter permite ejecutar código si los datos no son de confianza, y no tiene arreglo. Se marcó obsoleto en .NET 5 (SYSLIB0011) y en .NET 9 la implementación incluida siempre lanza una excepción.
porque.en: Deserializing with BinaryFormatter allows code execution when data is untrusted, and it cannot be fixed. It was marked obsolete in .NET 5 (SYSLIB0011) and in .NET 9 the in-box implementation always throws.

evidencia.titulo: Breaking change: BinaryFormatter serialization methods are obsolete and prohibited in ASP.NET apps (.NET 5)
evidencia.cita: Due to security vulnerabilities in BinaryFormatter, the following methods are now obsolete and produce a compile-time warning with ID SYSLIB0011.
BinaryFormatter is insecure and can't be made secure.

evidencia.titulo: Breaking change: In-box BinaryFormatter implementation removed and always throws (.NET 9)
evidencia.cita: The "in box" BinaryFormatter implementation now throws exceptions at runtime in all cases.

nota.es: .NET 5 marca Serialize/Deserialize como obsoletos (aviso SYSLIB0011) por sus vulnerabilidades.
nota.en: .NET 5 marks Serialize/Deserialize obsolete (SYSLIB0011 warning) because of its vulnerabilities.

nota.es: .NET 9 quita la implementación: siempre lanza una excepción en tiempo de ejecución.
nota.en: .NET 9 removes the implementation: it always throws at run time.

titulo.es: Bloquear código asíncrono con .Result, .Wait() o GetAwaiter().GetResult()
titulo.en: Blocking on async code with .Result, .Wait() or GetAwaiter().GetResult()

porque.es: En contextos con SynchronizationContext (WinForms, WPF, ASP.NET clásico) provoca interbloqueos; en ASP.NET Core agota el pool de hilos. Lo correcto es «async hasta arriba» (ver async-hasta-arriba-en-csharp).
porque.en: In contexts with a SynchronizationContext (WinForms, WPF, classic ASP.NET) it deadlocks; in ASP.NET Core it starves the thread pool. The fix is "async all the way" (see async-hasta-arriba-en-csharp).

evidencia.titulo: Async/Await - Best Practices in Asynchronous Programming (MSDN Magazine)

Do not block asynchronous execution by calling Task.Wait or Task<TResult>.Result.

evidencia.cita: A common performance problem in ASP.NET Core apps is blocking calls that could be asynchronous.

porque.es: Los agentes encuentran caminos válidos que el autor de la eval no previó, y el test los castiga. Anthropic (enero de 2026) dice que ese enfoque es demasiado rígido y da tests frágiles; mejor calificar lo que el agente produjo, con crédito parcial si la tarea tiene partes (ver calificar-el-estado-final-del-agente).
porque.en: Agents find valid paths the eval author did not foresee, and the test punishes them. Anthropic (January 2026) says this approach is too rigid and yields brittle tests; better to grade what the agent produced, with partial credit when the task has parts (ver calificar-el-estado-final-del-agente).

porque.es: La URL queda en el historial del navegador y en los logs del servidor. El token o la clave van en una cabecera (Authorization o una propia).
porque.en: The URL ends up in browser history and server logs. The token or key goes in a header (Authorization or a custom one).

evidencia.cita: Bearer tokens SHOULD NOT be passed in page URLs (for example, as query string parameters).

evidencia.cita: Passwords, security tokens, and API keys should not appear in the URL, as this can be captured in web server logs, which makes them intrinsically valuable.

nota.es: RFC 6750 (OAuth 2.0) dice que los tokens no deben ir en la URL: acaban en el historial del navegador y en los logs del servidor.
nota.en: RFC 6750 (OAuth 2.0) says tokens should not go in the URL: they end up in browser history and server logs.

nota.es: La hoja de OWASP sobre REST pide no poner contraseñas, tokens ni claves de API en la URL (fecha de entrada del texto en su repositorio).

titulo.es: Comprobar el texto libre que genera el LLM con igualdad exacta o un snapshot de la respuesta esperada
titulo.en: Checking free-form LLM text with exact equality or a snapshot of the expected answer

porque.es: Una respuesta abierta tiene muchas formas válidas, así que el test falla por cambios de redacción y no por errores reales. Anthropic (enero de 2026) avisa de que los graders de cadena son frágiles ante variaciones válidas; Opus 4.5 sacó un 42 % en CORE-Bench, en parte porque se penalizaba «96.12» frente a «96.124991…», y subió al 95 % al corregir la calificación y el andamiaje. La igualdad exacta sí vale para respuestas cerradas (una clase, un número); para el texto libre, combinar graders (ver combinar-graders-de-codigo-y-de-modelo).
porque.en: An open-ended answer has many valid forms, so the test fails on wording changes, not real errors. Anthropic (January 2026) warns that string graders are brittle to valid variations; Opus 4.5 scored 42% on CORE-Bench partly because “96.12” was penalised against “96.124991…”, rising to 95% once grading and scaffold were fixed. Exact match is still fine for closed answers (a label, a number); for free text, combine graders (ver combinar-graders-de-codigo-y-de-modelo).

evidencia.cita: Brittle to valid variations that don’t match expected patterns exactly

titulo.es: Dejar spring.jpa.open-in-view activado (el valor por defecto) para cargar asociaciones perezosas al pintar la vista
titulo.en: Leaving spring.jpa.open-in-view enabled (the default) to load lazy associations while rendering the view

porque.es: Con open-in-view activo (el valor por defecto) la sesión de Hibernate sigue abierta hasta el final de la petición y la vista puede lanzar consultas sin que se note. Spring Boot lo mantiene por compatibilidad pero desde la 2.0 (marzo de 2018) avisa en el arranque si no se decide explícitamente, y Hibernate recomienda cargar las asociaciones necesarias antes de cerrar el contexto de persistencia. Es una decisión, no un valor que dejar sin mirar.
porque.en: With open-in-view on (the default) the Hibernate session stays open until the end of the request and the view can trigger queries unnoticed. Spring Boot keeps it for compatibility but has warned at startup since 2.0 (March 2018) unless it is set explicitly, and Hibernate recommends fetching the needed associations before closing the persistence context. It is a decision, not a value to leave unexamined.

cuando.es: se deja el valor por defecto sin decidirlo, o una API serializa entidades con asociaciones perezosas
cuando.en: the default is left without a decision, or an API serialises entities with lazy associations

porque.es: Las consultas se disparan fuera de la capa de servicio sin que nadie lo vea; Hibernate aconseja cargar lo necesario antes (JOIN FETCH) y poner spring.jpa.open-in-view=false.
porque.en: Queries fire outside the service layer without anyone noticing; Hibernate advises fetching what is needed first (JOIN FETCH) and setting spring.jpa.open-in-view=false.

cuando.es: se activa explícitamente, a sabiendas de que la vista puede consultar la base de datos
cuando.en: it is enabled explicitly, knowing the view may query the database

porque.es: Spring Boot lo documenta como el patrón «Open EntityManager in View» para permitir la carga perezosa en las vistas; su equipo decidió no cambiar el valor por defecto.
porque.en: Spring Boot documents it as the «Open EntityManager in View» pattern to allow lazy loading in web views; its team decided not to change the default.

evidencia.cita: From now on, applications that don't explicitly enable `spring.jpa.open-in-view` will get a WARN message during startup.
This message makes sure that you understand that database queries may be performed during view rendering.
Spring Boot 2.0 is now generally available

evidencia.titulo: Hibernate ORM 7.0 User Guide — Best Practices (docs.jboss.org)
evidencia.cita: The best way to deal with LazyInitializationException is to fetch all the required associations prior to closing the Persistence Context.
Spring Boot by default registers OpenEntityManagerInViewInterceptor to apply the “Open EntityManager in View” pattern, to allow for lazy loading in web views.

evidencia.cita: If we were starting from a clean slate we may well have picked a different default, but we think the pain of changing the default (even at a major release) is going to cause more bugs than leaving things as they are.

titulo.es: Escribir las pruebas end-to-end con Playwright o Cypress (esperas automáticas y aserciones que reintentan)
titulo.en: Writing end-to-end tests with Playwright or Cypress (auto-waiting and retrying assertions)

porque.es: Esperan solas a que el elemento esté listo y reintentan las aserciones, lo que quita la mayor parte de la inestabilidad de las pruebas de interfaz. Tras retirar Protractor, «ng e2e» de Angular ofrece Cypress y Playwright entre sus opciones (junto a Nightwatch, WebdriverIO y Puppeteer).
porque.en: They wait for elements to be ready and retry assertions, which removes most UI-test flakiness. After dropping Protractor, Angular's `ng e2e` offers Cypress and Playwright among its options (alongside Nightwatch, WebdriverIO and Puppeteer).

evidencia.cita: In Cypress, you almost never need to use `cy.wait()` for an arbitrary amount of time.
Playwright waits until all the relevant actionability checks pass before performing an action.
Most of the time, web pages show information asynchronously, and using non-retrying assertions can lead to a flaky test.
Protractor was marked end-of-life in August 2023 (see https://protractortest.org/). Projects still relying on Protractor should consider migrating to another E2E testing framework
Playwright also extends it with convenience async matchers that will wait until the expected condition is met.
If it can't locate it, the CLI will then prompt you which e2e package you would like to use and walk you through the setup.

nota.es: La guía de buenas prácticas de Cypress ya pide esperar a condiciones explícitas, no a tiempos fijos.
nota.en: Cypress's best-practices guide already asks to wait for explicit conditions, not fixed times.

nota.es: Playwright 1.5 documenta las comprobaciones de «actionability»: espera a que se cumplan antes de cada acción.
nota.en: Playwright 1.5 documents actionability checks: it waits for them to pass before every action.

porque.en: Since September 2020 Moment has considered itself a legacy project in maintenance mode and discourages its use in new projects; existing ones may keep it. It reaffirmed this in August 2026 (see fechas-con-temporal-o-intl).

evidencia.cita: We now generally consider Moment to be a legacy project in maintenance mode. It is not dead, but it is indeed done.
existing projects may continue to use Moment, but we would like to discourage Moment from being used in new projects going forward.
The spirit of our 2020 message has not changed: Moment is a legacy project, and stability for existing users matters more than expanding its scope.
For that reason, maintenance mode no longer categorically rules out Moment 3.0.

nota.es: Moment pasa a modo mantenimiento, desaconseja usarlo en proyectos nuevos y recomienda alternativas y Temporal.
nota.en: Moment enters maintenance mode, discourages use in new projects and recommends alternatives and Temporal.

nota.es: Nueva nota de estado: sigue siendo un proyecto heredado; no descarta una 3.0 solo de mantenimiento.
nota.en: New status note: it remains a legacy project; a maintenance-only 3.0 is no longer ruled out.

titulo.es: Manejar fechas con Temporal e Intl (o una librería inmutable como Luxon o date-fns)
titulo.en: Handling dates with Temporal and Intl (or an immutable library such as Luxon or date-fns)

porque.es: Temporal llegó a stage 4 en TC39 en marzo de 2026 y ya viene en Firefox 139, Chrome 144 y Node.js 26. Safari aún no lo trae (solo en Technology Preview a fecha de revisión): ahí hace falta un polyfill, o Intl más una librería inmutable (ver fechas-con-moment-js-en-proyectos-nuevos).
porque.en: Temporal reached TC39 stage 4 in March 2026 and already ships in Firefox 139, Chrome 144 and Node.js 26. Safari does not ship it yet (only in Technology Preview as of review): there you need a polyfill, or Intl plus an immutable library (see fechas-con-moment-js-en-proyectos-nuevos).

evidencia.cita: We would also like to promote the Temporal addition to the JavaScript language, which is looking for feedback and contributors.
The Temporal API is now supported, this aims to simplify working with dates and times in various scenarios, with built-in time zone and calendar representations
The Temporal API in ECMA262 is a new API that provides standard objects and functions for working with dates and times.

evidencia.titulo: TC39 meeting notes, 11 March 2026 — Temporal for Stage 4
evidencia.cita: Temporal advances to stage 4.
This proposal is currently Stage 4.
The Temporal API is now enabled by default in Node.js 26.

porque.es: Go 1.24 (febrero de 2025) añadió la directiva tool en go.mod (go get -tool, go tool), que elimina el truco de tools.go (ver directiva-tool-en-go-mod).
porque.en: Go 1.24 (February 2025) added the tool directive in go.mod (go get -tool, go tool), which removes the tools.go workaround (see directiva-tool-en-go-mod).

evidencia.cita: I think the tools.go file is in fact the best practice for tool dependencies, certainly for Go 1.11.

evidencia.titulo: Go Wiki: Go Modules — How can I track tool dependencies for a module?
evidencia.cita: Before Go 1.24 the recommended approach was to add a tools.go file to your module that includes import statements for the tools of interest

Go modules can now track executable dependencies using tool directives in go.mod. This removes the need for the previous workaround of adding tools as blank imports to a file conventionally named "tools.go".

nota.es: Russ Cox, en la incidencia de Go sobre dependencias de herramientas, da el fichero tools.go como la mejor práctica para Go 1.11; la wiki de módulos lo recogió como lo recomendado hasta Go 1.24.

titulo.es: Fijar a mano el dialecto de Hibernate (hibernate.dialect o spring.jpa.database-platform)
titulo.en: Setting the Hibernate dialect by hand (hibernate.dialect or spring.jpa.database-platform)

porque.es: Desde Spring Boot 2.2 (2019) es Hibernate quien elige el dialecto, y Spring aconseja quitar la configuración que hubiera; desde Hibernate 6 (marzo de 2022) lo detecta solo a partir de la base de datos. La única razón que da Hibernate para fijarlo es usar una clase Dialect propia.
porque.en: Since Spring Boot 2.2 (2019) Hibernate chooses the dialect, and Spring advises removing any previous configuration; since Hibernate 6 (March 2022) it detects it on its own from the database. The only reason Hibernate gives to set it is using a custom Dialect class.

evidencia.cita: Spring Boot now lets Hibernate chose the dialect to use rather than applying a default dialect based on the detected database.
If you had a dialect configured previously, you may want to remove your customization.
Spring Boot 2.2.0 has been released
Since Hibernate 6, you don't need to specify hibernate.dialect.
The correct Hibernate SQL Dialect will be determined for you automatically. The only reason to specify this property is if you're using a custom user-written Dialect class.

nota.es: Spring Boot 2.2 deja que Hibernate elija el dialecto y aconseja quitar la configuración anterior.
nota.en: Spring Boot 2.2 lets Hibernate choose the dialect and advises removing previous configuration.

nota.es: Hibernate 6.0 detecta el dialecto solo (fecha del tag 6.0.0); su documentación dice que ya no hace falta indicarlo.
nota.en: Hibernate 6.0 detects the dialect on its own (date of the 6.0.0 tag); its documentation says it no longer needs to be specified.

porque.en: The filter stripped tags in its own way, not like strip_tags(). PHP 8.1 (November 2021) deprecates it and the manual says to use htmlspecialchars() instead (see escapar-la-salida-con-htmlspecialchars).

Strip tags, optionally strip or encode special characters.

nota.en: PHP 8.1 deprecates it; alternative: htmlspecialchars() on output.

titulo.es: Firmar commits y etiquetas con una clave SSH (`gpg.format ssh`) en vez de montar GPG
titulo.en: Signing commits and tags with an SSH key (`gpg.format ssh`) instead of setting up GPG

porque.es: Git firma con claves SSH desde la 2.34 (noviembre de 2021; la doc pide evitar OpenSSH 8.7), GitHub verifica esas firmas desde agosto de 2022 y GitLab también las verifica. Se puede reutilizar una clave SSH que ya tienes o crear una solo para firmar, sin montar GPG.
porque.en: Git signs with SSH keys since 2.34 (November 2021; the notes say to avoid OpenSSH 8.7), GitHub verifies those signatures since August 2022 and GitLab verifies them too. You can reuse an existing SSH key or create one just for signing, without setting up GPG.

evidencia.cita: In addition to GnuPG, ssh public crypto can be used for object and push-cert signing.  Note that this feature cannot be used with ssh-keygen from OpenSSH 8.7, whose support for it is broken.

evidencia.titulo: GitHub Docs: Telling Git about your signing key
evidencia.cita: You can use an existing SSH key to sign commits and tags, or generate a new one specifically for signing.

evidencia.titulo: GitLab Docs: Sign commits and tags with SSH keys
evidencia.cita: When you sign commits or tags with SSH keys, GitLab uses the SSH public keys associated with your GitLab account to cryptographically verify the signature.

evidencia.titulo: GitHub Changelog: SSH commit verification now supported
evidencia.cita: GitHub now supports SSH commit verification, so you can sign commits and tags locally using a self-generated SSH public key

nota.es: Git 2.34 admite claves SSH para firmar (no con el ssh-keygen de OpenSSH 8.7).
nota.en: Git 2.34 supports SSH keys for signing (not with OpenSSH 8.7's ssh-keygen).

nota.es: GitHub empieza a verificar commits y etiquetas firmados con SSH.
nota.en: GitHub starts verifying commits and tags signed with SSH.

nota.en: Documented as of review date: GitHub and GitLab explain how to sign with SSH and verify it.

titulo.es: Compilar C y C++ con -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2
titulo.en: Compiling C and C++ with -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2

porque.es: El nivel 3 hace las mismas comprobaciones que el 2 y además protege muchas más llamadas, porque también usa tamaños que el compilador solo conoce como expresión. Funciona con glibc 2.35 y GCC 12 (2022); OpenSSF lo recomienda desde 2023 y Ubuntu lo pone por defecto desde 2024.
porque.en: Level 3 does the same checks as level 2 and protects many more calls, because it also uses sizes the compiler only knows as an expression. It works with glibc 2.35 and GCC 12 (2022); OpenSSF has recommended it since 2023 and Ubuntu has defaulted to it since 2024.

evidencia.titulo: dpkg (Debian), debian/changelog: versión 1.16.1.1 (2011-10-14), repositorio del mantenedor (Guillem Jover)
evidencia.cita: Change dpkg-buildflags to set preprocessor option -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 in CPPFLAGS, instead of CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS.
Source fortification (_FORTIFY_SOURCE) level 3 is now available for applications compiling with glibc and gcc 12 and later.

evidencia.titulo: OpenSSF, Compiler Options Hardening Guide for C and C++ (versión de la publicación inicial, commit 4eccd36 del 2023-11-29)
evidencia.cita: Same checks as in `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2`, but with significantly more calls fortified with a potential to impact performance in some rare cases

evidencia.titulo: dpkg (Debian), debian/changelog: versión 1.22.3 (2024-01-19), repositorio del mantenedor (Guillem Jover)
evidencia.cita: Dpkg::Vendor::Ubuntu: Default to fortify level 3.

nota.es: Las distribuciones compilan sus paquetes con -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 (dpkg-buildflags de Debian).
nota.en: Distributions build their packages with -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 (Debian's dpkg-buildflags).

nota.es: glibc 2.35: el nivel 3 está disponible con GCC 12 (GCC 12.1 sale el 2022-05-06).
nota.en: glibc 2.35: level 3 is available with GCC 12 (GCC 12.1 is released on 2022-05-06).

nota.es: La guía de OpenSSF recomienda -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3.
nota.en: The OpenSSF guide recommends -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3.

nota.en: dpkg 1.22.3 makes level 3 the default on Ubuntu.

titulo.es: Compilar C y C++ con -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 (y al menos -O1)
titulo.en: Compiling C and C++ with -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 (and at least -O1)

porque.es: Detecta desbordamientos en muchas más llamadas a la libc que el nivel 2. Necesita glibc 2.35 y GCC 12 o Clang 9, y al menos -O1; desde GCC 14 viene incluido en -fhardened (que cae al nivel 2 si la glibc es anterior a la 2.35).
porque.en: It catches overflows in many more libc calls than level 2. It needs glibc 2.35 and GCC 12 or Clang 9, and at least -O1; since GCC 14 it is included in -fhardened (which falls back to level 2 if glibc is older than 2.35).

evidencia.cita: Source fortification (_FORTIFY_SOURCE) level 3 is now available for applications compiling with glibc and gcc 12 and later.

evidencia.titulo: OpenSSF, Compiler Options Hardening Guide for C and C++ (versión de la publicación inicial, commit 4eccd36 del 2023-11-29)
evidencia.cita: Same checks as in `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2`, but with significantly more calls fortified with a potential to impact performance in some rare cases

evidencia.titulo: Manual de GCC 14.1, Program Instrumentation Options: -fhardened (GCC 14.1 publicado el 2024-05-07)
evidencia.cita: When the system glibc is older than 2.35, -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 is used instead.

nota.es: glibc 2.35 habilita el nivel 3 con GCC 12.
nota.en: glibc 2.35 enables level 3 with GCC 12.

nota.es: OpenSSF lo incluye en su lista de opciones recomendadas.
nota.en: OpenSSF includes it in its list of recommended options.

nota.es: GCC 14.1: -fhardened activa -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 entre otras opciones.
nota.en: GCC 14.1: -fhardened turns on -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 among other options.

titulo.en: Loading classes by defining the __autoload() function

porque.en: It was deprecated in PHP 7.2 (2017) and removed in PHP 8.0 (2020). Register the loader with spl_autoload_register(), which is what Composer's autoloader does (see autoload-psr-4-con-composer).

evidencia.cita: The __autoload() interceptor function will be automatically called when an undeclared class is to be instantiated.
The __autoload() mechanism has been deprecated, use spl_autoload_register() instead.
Removed ability to specify an autoloader using an __autoload() function. spl_autoload_register() should be used instead.

nota.en: PHP 7.2 deprecates it in favour of spl_autoload_register().

porque.en: PHP has anonymous functions since 5.3 (June 2009) and arrow functions since 7.4 (November 2019). They are what PHP says to use instead of create_function(), and foreach instead of each() (see create-function-y-each).

evidencia.cita: Added lambda functions and closures.
The create_function() function has been deprecated, use anonymous functions instead.
The each() function has been deprecated, use a foreach loop instead.

titulo.en: Accessing MySQL with the mysql_* functions (mysql_connect, mysql_query…)

porque.en: The mysql extension was deprecated in PHP 5.5 (June 2013) and removed in PHP 7.0 (December 2015): the code does not even run. Move to mysqli or PDO, with prepared statements (see pdo-o-mysqli-con-consultas-preparadas).

evidencia.cita: Unless you specify a path to --with-mysql, the bundled MySQL client library will be used

The original MySQL extension is now deprecated, and will generate deprecation warnings when connecting to a database through mysql_connect(), mysql_pconnect() or by establishing an implicit connection. Use MySQLi or PDO instead.

evidencia.cita: This extension is deprecated as of PHP 5.5.0, and has been removed as of PHP 7.0.0. Instead, either the mysqli or PDO_MySQL extension should be used.

titulo.es: Usar `git checkout` para todo: cambiar de rama y descartar cambios en ficheros
titulo.en: Using `git checkout` for everything: switching branches and discarding file changes

porque.es: `git checkout` mezcla dos operaciones distintas: cambiar de rama y sacar ficheros del índice o de un commit. Git 2.23 (agosto de 2019) las separó en `git switch` y `git restore`, que nacieron experimentales y dejaron de serlo en Git 2.51 (agosto de 2025).
porque.en: `git checkout` mixes two different operations: switching branches and checking out files from the index or a commit. Git 2.23 (August 2019) split them into `git switch` and `git restore`, which started out experimental and stopped being so in Git 2.51 (August 2025).

evidencia.cita: $ git checkout experimental

Two new commands "git switch" and "git restore" are introduced to split "checking out a branch to work on advancing its history" and "checking out paths out of the index and/or a tree-ish to work on advancing the current history" out of the single "git checkout" command.
"git switch" and "git restore" are declared to be no longer experimental.
THIS COMMAND IS EXPERIMENTAL. THE BEHAVIOR MAY CHANGE.

nota.es: El tutorial oficial de Git 2.22 cambia de rama con `git checkout`, la orden que servía tanto para ramas como para restaurar ficheros.
nota.en: The official Git 2.22 tutorial switches branches with `git checkout`, the command used both for branches and for restoring files.

nota.es: Git 2.23 añade `git switch` y `git restore`, todavía marcadas como experimentales; `git checkout` sigue siendo lo normal.
nota.en: Git 2.23 adds `git switch` and `git restore`, still marked experimental; `git checkout` remains the norm.

nota.es: Git 2.51 declara estables `git switch` y `git restore`. `git checkout` sigue funcionando, pero para lo nuevo se usan las órdenes separadas.
nota.en: Git 2.51 declares `git switch` and `git restore` stable. `git checkout` still works, but new usage relies on the separate commands.

titulo.es: Organizar las ramas con git-flow (develop, release, hotfix…)
titulo.en: Organising branches with git-flow (develop, release, hotfix…)

porque.es: Su propio autor lo matizó en 2020: no lo pensó para software que se despliega de forma continua, y ahí recomienda un flujo mucho más simple. Para software con versiones o con varias versiones en uso, dice que puede seguir encajando.
porque.en: Its own author qualified it in 2020: he did not design it for continuously delivered software, where he recommends a much simpler flow. For versioned software or several versions in use, he says it may still fit.

cuando.es: el equipo despliega de forma continua (aplicaciones web, sin varias versiones en uso)
cuando.en: the team delivers continuously (web apps, no multiple versions in use)

porque.es: El autor propone un flujo más simple (como GitHub flow).
porque.en: The author proposes a simpler flow (such as GitHub flow).

cuando.es: el software tiene versiones explícitas o hay que mantener varias en uso
cuando.en: the software is explicitly versioned or several versions must be supported

evidencia.titulo: A successful Git branching model — Note of reflection (Vincent Driessen)
evidencia.cita: If your team is doing continuous delivery of software, I would suggest to adopt a much simpler workflow (like GitHub flow) instead of trying to shoehorn git-flow into your team.

evidencia.titulo: A successful Git branching model — Note of reflection (Vincent Driessen)
evidencia.cita: If, however, you are building software that is explicitly versioned, or if you need to support multiple versions of your software in the wild, then git-flow may still be as good of a fit to your team as it has been to people in the last 10 years.

evidencia.titulo: A successful Git branching model (Vincent Driessen)
evidencia.cita: In this post I present the development model that I’ve introduced for some of my projects

nota.es: Vincent Driessen publica el modelo.
nota.en: Vincent Driessen publishes the model.

nota.es: El autor añade una «nota de reflexión»: para entrega continua, mejor un flujo más simple.
nota.en: The author adds a "note of reflection": for continuous delivery, a simpler flow is better.

titulo.es: Reescribir una rama remota con `git push --force` (o `-f`)
titulo.en: Rewriting a remote branch with `git push --force` (or `-f`)

porque.es: `--force` desactiva la comprobación y, como avisa la propia documentación de Git, puede hacer que el remoto pierda commits. Desde Git 1.8.5 (noviembre de 2013) `--force-with-lease` ofrece un control más fino (ver git-push-force-with-lease); GitHub y GitLab lo usan en sus guías de rebase y GitLab desaconseja forzar en ramas compartidas.
porque.en: `--force` disables the check and, as Git's own documentation warns, can make the remote lose commits. Since Git 1.8.5 (November 2013) `--force-with-lease` offers finer control (see git-push-force-with-lease); GitHub and GitLab use it in their rebase guides and GitLab advises against force-pushing shared branches.

evidencia.cita: This flag disables the check. This can cause the remote repository to lose commits; use it with care.
"git push" learned a more fine grained control over a blunt "--force" when requesting a non-fast-forward update with the "--force-with-lease=<refname>:<expected object name>" option.

evidencia.titulo: GitLab Docs: Rebase to address merge conflicts
evidencia.cita: Force pushing is not recommended on shared branches, because you risk destroying others' changes.

evidencia.titulo: GitLab Docs: Rebase to address merge conflicts
evidencia.cita: Force push your changes to the target branch, while protecting others' commits:

evidencia.titulo: GitHub Docs: Using Git rebase on the command line
evidencia.cita: $ git push origin main --force-with-lease

nota.es: La documentación de `git push` de Git 1.8.4 solo ofrece `--force` para subir historia reescrita, y avisa de que puede perder commits.
nota.en: The Git 1.8.4 `git push` documentation only offers `--force` to push rewritten history, and warns it can lose commits.

nota.es: Git 1.8.5 añade `--force-with-lease`, un control más fino que el `--force` «a lo bruto».
nota.en: Git 1.8.5 adds `--force-with-lease`, a finer-grained control than a blunt `--force`.

nota.es: Documentado así a fecha de revisión: GitHub y GitLab usan `--force-with-lease` en sus guías de rebase, y GitLab desaconseja forzar en ramas compartidas.
nota.en: Documented as of review date: GitHub and GitLab use `--force-with-lease` in their rebase guides, and GitLab advises against force-pushing shared branches.

titulo.es: Subir historia reescrita con `git push --force-with-lease`
titulo.en: Pushing rewritten history with `git push --force-with-lease`

porque.es: Rechaza el push si la rama remota ya no está como esperabas, así no borras commits ajenos. Existe desde Git 1.8.5 (2013). Ojo: sin valor esperado, cualquier `git fetch` en segundo plano (un cron, el IDE) anula la protección; por eso conviene dar el valor esperado o añadir `--force-if-includes` (Git 2.30).
porque.en: It rejects the push if the remote branch is no longer as you expected, so you do not wipe out others' commits. Available since Git 1.8.5 (2013). Beware: without an expected value, any background `git fetch` (a cron job, the IDE) defeats the protection; so give the expected value or add `--force-if-includes` (Git 2.30).

evidencia.cita: "git push" learned a more fine grained control over a blunt "--force" when requesting a non-fast-forward update with the "--force-with-lease=<refname>:<expected object name>" option.

evidencia.titulo: GitLab Docs: Rebase to address merge conflicts
evidencia.cita: Force push your changes to the target branch, while protecting others' commits:

evidencia.titulo: GitHub Docs: Using Git rebase on the command line
evidencia.cita: $ git push origin main --force-with-lease
interacts very badly with anything that implicitly runs `git fetch` on the remote to be pushed to in the background, e.g. `git fetch origin` on your repository in a cronjob.
A new option "--force-if-includes" attempts to ensure that what is being force-pushed was created after examining the commit at the tip of the remote ref that is about to be force-replaced.

nota.es: Llega en Git 1.8.5.
nota.en: Arrives in Git 1.8.5.

nota.es: Git 2.30 añade `--force-if-includes`, porque `--force-with-lease` a secas puede perder commits si algo hace `git fetch` por detrás.
nota.en: Git 2.30 adds `--force-if-includes`, because bare `--force-with-lease` can lose commits if something runs `git fetch` behind your back.

nota.es: Documentado así a fecha de revisión: GitHub y GitLab la usan en sus guías de rebase, y la documentación de Git avisa del fetch en segundo plano.
nota.en: Documented as of review date: GitHub and GitLab use it in their rebase guides, and Git's documentation warns about background fetches.

porque.es: Por defecto una consulta puede anidar y pedir cantidades sin límite, lo que permite tumbar el servidor (DoS). OWASP y graphql.org piden limitar la profundidad y la cantidad.
porque.en: By default a query can nest and request unlimited amounts, which allows taking the server down (DoS). OWASP and graphql.org ask to limit depth and amount.

evidencia.titulo: GraphQL Cheat Sheet (OWASP; publicada el 2020-10-30, commit dc5b7d5103)
evidencia.cita: By default these can both be unlimited which may lead to a DoS. You should set limits on depth and amount to prevent DoS, but this usually requires a small custom implementation as it is not natively supported by GraphQL.
For this reason, it's a good idea to limit the maximum depth of fields that a single operation can have.

titulo.es: Inyectar las dependencias obligatorias por constructor (campos final)
titulo.en: Injecting mandatory dependencies through the constructor (final fields)

porque.es: La documentación de Spring la recomienda desde la 4.1 (2014) y sigue haciéndolo: objetos inmutables, dependencias no nulas y componentes completamente inicializados. El setter queda para dependencias opcionales.
porque.en: The Spring documentation has recommended it since 4.1 (2014) and still does: immutable objects, non-null dependencies and fully initialised components. Setters are left for optional dependencies.

evidencia.cita: The Spring team generally advocates constructor injection as it enables one to implement application components as _immutable objects_ and to ensure that required dependencies are not `null`.
The Spring team generally advocates constructor injection, as it lets you implement application components as immutable objects and ensures that required dependencies are not null.
Furthermore, constructor-injected components are always returned to the client (calling) code in a fully initialized state.
Setter injection should primarily only be used for optional dependencies that can be assigned reasonable default values within the class.

evidencia.cita: The Spring team generally advocates setter injection, because large numbers of constructor arguments can get unwieldy, especially when properties are optional.

titulo.es: Pedir al juez LLM una nota de 1 a 10 sin rúbrica y usarla como umbral en el CI
titulo.en: Asking the LLM judge for a 1–10 score without a rubric and using it as a CI threshold

porque.es: Las escalas finas sin anclas dan notas inconsistentes entre ejecuciones y la frontera «7 aprueba, 6 suspende» es arbitraria. promptfoo (abril de 2026) recomienda pasa/no pasa para las puertas y escalas de baja precisión (binaria o de 3 puntos); Anthropic pide rúbricas detalladas y salida «correct»/«incorrect» o, como mucho, 1–5. La alternativa es un juez binario con rúbrica (ver juez-llm-binario-con-rubrica); los sesgos de orden y de autopreferencia, aparte (ver llm-como-juez-sin-mitigar-sesgos).
porque.en: Fine-grained scales without anchors give inconsistent scores across runs, and the “7 passes, 6 fails” cut-off is arbitrary. promptfoo (April 2026) recommends pass/fail for gates and low-precision scales (binary or 3-point); Anthropic asks for detailed rubrics and “correct”/“incorrect” output or, at most, 1–5. The alternative is a binary judge with a rubric (ver juez-llm-binario-con-rubrica); order and self-preference biases are separate (ver llm-como-juez-sin-mitigar-sesgos).

evidencia.titulo: Demystifying evals for AI agents (Anthropic Engineering)
evidencia.cita: It can also help to create clear, structured rubrics to grade each dimension of a task, and then grade each dimension with an isolated LLM-as-judge rather than using one to grade all dimensions.

evidencia.cita: Using this macro, it is possible to have statics that require code to be executed at runtime in order to be initialized.

porque.es: Un método async void no devuelve Task: sus excepciones no se pueden capturar con try/catch del llamador y no se puede esperar a que termine. Solo se justifica en manejadores de eventos. Lo correcto es devolver Task (ver async-hasta-arriba-en-csharp).

titulo.es: Usar multiprocessing (procesos) para paralelizar código Python puro de CPU porque el GIL impide hacerlo con hilos
titulo.en: Using multiprocessing (processes) to parallelize pure-Python CPU code because the GIL prevents doing it with threads

porque.es: Con el GIL, los hilos no ejecutan bytecode Python en paralelo y por eso se usan procesos. PEP 703 (aceptado en octubre de 2023) hace el GIL opcional: Python 3.13 (2024) trajo una compilación sin GIL experimental y Python 3.14 (octubre de 2025) la declaró soportada pero no predeterminada. En el Python normal los procesos siguen siendo la vía; en la compilación sin GIL, los hilos ya paralelizan.
porque.en: Under the GIL, threads do not run Python bytecode in parallel, which is why processes are used. PEP 703 (accepted in October 2023) makes the GIL optional: Python 3.13 (2024) brought an experimental GIL-free build and Python 3.14 (October 2025) declared it supported but not the default. On regular Python processes remain the way; on the free-threaded build, threads already run in parallel.

cuando.es: Python estándar (con GIL), que es el predeterminado, o dependencias con extensiones C que no declaran soporte de free-threading (al importarlas se reactiva el GIL)
cuando.en: standard Python (with GIL), the default, or dependencies with C extensions that do not declare free-threading support (importing them re-enables the GIL)

porque.es: Solo un hilo ejecuta bytecode Python a la vez; multiprocessing usa procesos separados para esquivar el GIL.
porque.en: Only one thread runs Python bytecode at a time; multiprocessing uses separate processes to bypass the GIL.

cuando.es: compilación free-threaded de Python 3.14+ (python3.14t) con dependencias compatibles
cuando.en: free-threaded build of Python 3.14+ (python3.14t) with compatible dependencies

porque.es: Los hilos corren en paralelo y comparten memoria, sin serializar datos entre procesos; a cambio, el código de un solo hilo va en torno a un 5–10 % más lento.
porque.en: Threads run in parallel and share memory, without serializing data between processes; in exchange, single-threaded code is about 5–10% slower.

evidencia.cita: Unlike the multiprocessing module, which uses separate processes to bypass the global interpreter lock (GIL), the threading module operates within a single process, meaning that all threads share the same memory space.
As of Python 3.13, free-threaded builds can disable the GIL, enabling true parallel execution of threads, but this feature is not available by default (see PEP 703).

The free-threaded build of Python is now supported and no longer experimental.
The performance penalty on single-threaded code in free-threaded mode is now roughly 5-10%, depending on the platform and C compiler used.

titulo.es: Crear y desechar un HttpClient nuevo en cada petición (using var client = new HttpClient())

porque.es: Cada HttpClient lleva su propio pool de conexiones; crearlo y desecharlo por petición agota los puertos con carga alta. La guía oficial pide reutilizarlo o usar IHttpClientFactory (ver reutilizar-httpclient-o-ihttpclientfactory).
porque.en: Each HttpClient carries its own connection pool; creating and disposing one per request exhausts ports under load. The official guidance says to reuse it or use IHttpClientFactory (see reutilizar-httpclient-o-ihttpclientfactory).

evidencia.cita: includes a new IHttpClientFactory service that makes it easier to configure and consume instances of HttpClient in apps.
To avoid port exhaustion problems, reuse HttpClient instances for as many HTTP requests as possible.
What matters is that they're not created and disposed with each request, as they each contain a connection pool.
Instantiating an HttpClient class for every request will exhaust the number of sockets available under heavy loads.
IHttpClientFactory – HttpClient client as a service that you can centrally manage and configure.

nota.es: La referencia de HttpClient avisa: instanciarlo en cada petición agota los sockets con carga alta (fecha de la versión de docs; el aviso viene de MSDN).

titulo.es: Optimizar automáticamente los prompts de un pipeline con DSPy (MIPROv2, GEPA) en vez de retocarlos a mano
titulo.en: Automatically optimising a pipeline's prompts with DSPy (MIPROv2, GEPA) instead of hand-tuning them

porque.es: DSPy 3.0 (agosto de 2025) trajo GEPA, que usa la crítica en texto de una métrica para proponer prompts con pocas ejecuciones; MIPROv2 pide unos 200 ejemplos o más para no sobreajustar, y con unos 10 la documentación aconseja empezar por BootstrapFewShot. Compensa si hay métrica automática y datos; si no, basta ajustar a mano contra las evals (ver evaluar-con-un-conjunto-de-evals) o pedir al modelo que mejore el prompt (ver pedir-al-modelo-que-escriba-el-prompt).
porque.en: DSPy 3.0 (August 2025) brought GEPA, which uses a metric's textual feedback to propose prompts in few rollouts; MIPROv2 needs about 200 examples or more to avoid overfitting, and with around 10 the docs advise starting with BootstrapFewShot. It pays off when there is an automatic metric and data; otherwise hand-tuning against evals (ver evaluar-con-un-conjunto-de-evals) or asking the model to improve the prompt (ver pedir-al-modelo-que-escriba-el-prompt) is enough.

cuando.es: Pipeline de varios pasos con LLM, métrica automática fiable y decenas o cientos de ejemplos etiquetados
cuando.en: Multi-step LLM pipeline with a reliable automatic metric and tens or hundreds of labelled examples

porque.es: El optimizador explora instrucciones y ejemplos de cada paso mejor que el ajuste manual, y se repite al cambiar de modelo.
porque.en: The optimiser explores each step's instructions and examples better than manual tuning, and can be re-run when the model changes.

cuando.es: Un solo prompt, sin métrica automática o con muy pocos ejemplos
cuando.en: A single prompt, no automatic metric or very few examples

porque.es: Sin señal fiable el optimizador sobreajusta; basta iterar a mano contra un conjunto pequeño de evals.
porque.en: Without a reliable signal the optimiser overfits; iterating by hand against a small eval set is enough.

evidencia.cita: This allows GEPA to propose high performing prompts in very few rollouts.
If you have **very few examples** (around 10), start with `BootstrapFewShot`.
and have enough data (e.g. 200 examples or more to prevent overfitting) then try `MIPROv2`.
a new optimizer that builds a Pareto tree of prompts, uses NL reflection to extract/validate lessons, and can produce shorter prompts while improving downstream performance.

titulo.es: Paginar una API con offset/limit (o número de página)

porque.es: Offset es sencillo y permite saltar a la página N, pero con muchos datos tiene problemas de rendimiento y, si se añaden filas entre petición y petición, las páginas siguientes se vuelven ambiguas. Para listas grandes o vivas se usan cursores opacos.
porque.en: Offset is simple and allows jumping to page N, but with large data sets it has performance downsides and, if rows are added between requests, later pages become ambiguous. Large or live lists use opaque cursors.

cuando.es: listas pequeñas y estables, o paneles internos que necesitan ir a la página N
cuando.en: small, stable lists, or internal dashboards that need to jump to page N

porque.es: El coste de offset es bajo y es lo más simple.
porque.en: Offset cost is low and it is the simplest option.

cuando.es: listas grandes o que cambian a menudo (feeds, scroll infinito, APIs públicas)
cuando.en: large or frequently changing lists (feeds, infinite scroll, public APIs)

porque.es: Con cursores opacos no hay páginas ambiguas cuando cambian los datos, y graphql.org la considera la opción más potente.
porque.en: With opaque cursors pages do not become ambiguous when data changes, and graphql.org considers it the most powerful option.

porque.en: PATCH applies partial changes and has existed since 2010 (RFC 5789). The body is usually a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396), designed for PATCH; PUT is for replacing the whole resource (see put-para-actualizaciones-parciales).

evidencia.cita: This proposal adds a new HTTP method, PATCH, to modify an existing HTTP resource.
The merge patch format is primarily intended for use with the HTTP PATCH method as a means of describing a set of modifications to a target resource's content.
The PATCH HTTP method applies partial modifications to a resource.

nota.es: RFC 5789 añade el método PATCH para modificar un recurso existente.
nota.en: RFC 5789 adds the PATCH method to modify an existing resource.

nota.es: RFC 7396 define JSON Merge Patch, pensado para enviarse con PATCH.
nota.en: RFC 7396 defines JSON Merge Patch, intended to be sent with PATCH.

titulo.es: Hacer «pip install» en el Python del sistema operativo (o forzarlo con --break-system-packages)
titulo.en: Running "pip install" into the operating system Python (or forcing it with --break-system-packages)

porque.es: Mezcla los paquetes de pip con los del gestor del sistema y puede romper herramientas del propio SO. PEP 668 deja que una distribución marque su Python como «externally managed», y desde pip 23.0 (enero de 2023) pip se niega a instalar en él fuera de un entorno virtual (ver instalar-en-un-entorno-virtual).
porque.en: It mixes pip packages with the OS package manager's and can break the OS's own tools. PEP 668 lets a distribution mark its Python as "externally managed", and since pip 23.0 (January 2023) pip refuses to install into it outside a virtual environment (see instalar-en-un-entorno-virtual).

evidencia.titulo: PEP 668 – Marking Python base environments as “externally managed”
evidencia.cita: a better solution for most (but not all) use cases is to use Python-specific package management tools only within a virtual environment.
Implement logic to read the EXTERNALLY-MANAGED file as specified in PEP 668.

nota.es: Se crea PEP 668: las herramientas no deben instalar en el entorno global que gestiona el sistema y deben llevar al usuario a un entorno virtual.
nota.en: PEP 668 is created: tools must not install into the system-managed global environment and should steer users to a virtual environment.

nota.es: pip 23.0 lee el marcador EXTERNALLY-MANAGED de PEP 668 y se niega a instalar en esos Python.
nota.en: pip 23.0 reads the PEP 668 EXTERNALLY-MANAGED marker and refuses to install into those Pythons.

titulo.es: Envolver errores en Go con github.com/pkg/errors (errors.Wrap, errors.Cause)
titulo.en: Wrapping Go errors with github.com/pkg/errors (errors.Wrap, errors.Cause)

porque.es: Go 1.13 (septiembre de 2019) añadió %w en fmt.Errorf y errors.Is/As/Unwrap a la biblioteca estándar, y Go 1.20 añadió errors.Join (ver envolver-errores-con-fmt-errorf-w-en-go). pkg/errors anunció en enero de 2019 que pasaba a modo mantenimiento.
porque.en: Go 1.13 (September 2019) added %w in fmt.Errorf and errors.Is/As/Unwrap to the standard library, and Go 1.20 added errors.Join (see envolver-errores-con-fmt-errorf-w-en-go). pkg/errors announced in January 2019 that it was moving into maintenance mode.

evidencia.cita: The errors package allows programmers to add context to the failure path in their code in a way that does not destroy the original value of the error.
With the upcoming Go2 error proposals this package is moving into maintenance mode.

To support wrapping, fmt.Errorf now has a %w verb for creating wrapped errors, and three new functions in the errors package ( errors.Unwrap, errors.Is and errors.As) simplify unwrapping and inspecting wrapped errors.
The new function errors.Join returns an error wrapping a list of errors.

nota.es: pkg/errors 0.8.0: añade contexto a los errores sin perder el original, algo que la biblioteca estándar aún no ofrece.
nota.en: pkg/errors 0.8.0: adds context to errors without losing the original, something the standard library does not yet offer.

nota.es: El propio paquete anuncia que pasará a modo mantenimiento ante las propuestas de errores de Go 2.
nota.en: The package itself announces it will move into maintenance mode given the Go 2 error proposals.

nota.es: Go 1.13 incorpora el envoltorio de errores a la biblioteca estándar.
nota.en: Go 1.13 brings error wrapping into the standard library.

titulo.es: Fijar un porcentaje de cobertura de código (80 %, 100 %) como objetivo o requisito para aceptar cambios
titulo.en: Setting a code-coverage percentage (80%, 100%) as a goal or merge requirement

porque.es: La cobertura dice qué líneas se ejecutaron, no si se comprobó algo, y convertida en meta el equipo la trata como techo. Google desaconseja imponer un porcentaje de arriba abajo, pero sí ve razonable un umbral alto para el código de cada cambio (ver tests-de-mutacion-para-tests-generados-por-ia).
porque.en: Coverage says which lines ran, not whether anything was checked, and once it becomes a target teams treat it as a ceiling. Google advises against top-down percentage mandates but considers a high threshold for each change's code reasonable (see tests-de-mutacion-para-tests-generados-por-ia).

cuando.es: Un porcentaje global impuesto de arriba abajo, igual para todos los equipos, como nota de la calidad de los tests
cuando.en: A global percentage mandated top-down, the same for every team, as a grade of test quality

porque.es: Se convierte en un fin en sí mismo: el 80 % pasa de suelo a techo y se escriben tests para el número.
porque.en: It becomes a goal unto itself: 80% turns from floor into ceiling and tests are written for the number.

cuando.es: Un umbral para el código nuevo o modificado en cada cambio, elegido por el equipo según lo crítico que sea, como señal de código sin probar
cuando.en: A threshold for new or changed code in each change, chosen by the team according to criticality, as a signal of untested code

porque.es: Google lo considera razonable (90 % como suelo por commit) para que los tests no empeoren con el tiempo.
porque.en: Google considers it reasonable (90% as a per-commit floor) so tests do not get worse over time.

evidencia.titulo: Software Engineering at Google, cap. 11: Testing Overview — A Note on Code Coverage
evidencia.cita: An even more insidious problem with code coverage is that, like other metrics, it quickly becomes a goal unto itself.

evidencia.titulo: Software Engineering at Google, cap. 11: Testing Overview — A Note on Code Coverage
evidencia.cita: In practice, what happens is that instead of treating 80% like a floor, engineers treat it like a ceiling.

evidencia.titulo: Google Testing Blog — Code Coverage Best Practices
evidencia.cita: However we like to stay away from broad top-down mandates and encourage every team to select the value that makes sense for their business needs.

evidencia.titulo: Google Testing Blog — Code Coverage Best Practices
evidencia.cita: While project wide goals above 90% are most likely not worth it, per-commit coverage goals of 99% are reasonable, and 90% is a good lower threshold.

nota.es: Google publica «Software Engineering at Google» (primera edición, O'Reilly): la cobertura como meta se convierte en techo.
nota.en: Google publishes "Software Engineering at Google" (first edition, O'Reilly): coverage as a goal turns into a ceiling.

nota.es: El blog de testing de Google matiza: nada de mandatos de arriba abajo, pero umbrales por commit (90 % como suelo) sí son razonables.
nota.en: Google's testing blog nuances it: no top-down mandates, but per-commit thresholds (90% as a floor) are reasonable.

porque.en: Promises remain the foundation of async/await. For a sequential flow, async/await reads like synchronous code and Node calls it one of the best ways to work with promises; to combine several (Promise.all, race, any) or for a one-off .catch, .then and .catch are still the norm.

The PATCH HTTP method applies partial modifications to a resource.

evidencia.cita: This library provides a convenient derive macro for the standard library's std::error::Error trait.
a trait object based error type for easy idiomatic error handling in Rust applications.

This is common in application code. Use [thiserror] if you

Anyhow is a good replacement for failure::Error.
thiserror is a good, near drop-in replacement for #[derive(Fail)].

porque.es: El tipo ?T existe desde PHP 7.1 (diciembre de 2016) y equivale a T|null. El manual desaconseja hacerlo nullable solo con «= null», y PHP 8.4 (noviembre de 2024) depreca esa forma (ver parametro-nullable-implicito).

evidencia.cita: Added nullable types.
A single base type declaration can be marked nullable by prefixing the type with a question mark (?). Thus ?T and T|null are identical.
Implicitly nullable parameter types are now deprecated.

titulo.es: Usar el OpenAI Agents SDK con datos personales o confidenciales dejando la traza tal como viene (activada y con entradas y salidas completas)
titulo.en: Using the OpenAI Agents SDK with personal or confidential data leaving tracing as shipped (on, with full inputs and outputs)

porque.es: Desde la primera versión (marzo de 2025) la traza está activada por defecto y los spans guardan las entradas y salidas del modelo y de las herramientas, que se ven en el panel de OpenAI; hoy la documentación dice además que trace_include_sensitive_data vale True por defecto. Hay que desactivarla (OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_TRACING=1), quitar los datos sensibles o mandarla a un backend propio; con retención cero (ZDR) ni siquiera está disponible. Es el caso concreto de capturar contenido del LLM sin opt-in (ver capturar-contenido-de-llm-con-opt-in-y-enmascarado).
porque.en: Since the first release (March 2025) tracing has been on by default and spans store model and tool inputs and outputs, visible in OpenAI's dashboard; today's docs also state that trace_include_sensitive_data is True by default. You must disable it (OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_TRACING=1), strip sensitive data or send it to your own backend; under Zero Data Retention (ZDR) it is not even available. It is the specific case of capturing LLM content without opt-in (ver capturar-contenido-de-llm-con-opt-in-y-enmascarado).

evidencia.cita: Tracing is enabled by default. There are two ways to disable tracing:
By default, trace_include_sensitive_data is True.
Tracing is unavailable for organizations that use OpenAI's APIs under a Zero Data Retention (ZDR) policy.
For example, the `generation_span()` stores the inputs/outputs of the LLM generation, and `function_span()` stores the inputs/outputs of function calls.

nota.es: openai-agents 0.0.3: la traza viene activada por defecto y sus spans guardan las entradas y salidas del modelo y de las funciones salvo que se desactive.
nota.en: openai-agents 0.0.3: tracing is on by default and its spans store model and function inputs and outputs unless disabled.

nota.es: Documentado así a fecha de revisión: trace_include_sensitive_data vale True por defecto y la traza no está disponible con ZDR.

titulo.es: Deserializar con pickle (o con joblib.load o torch.load, que lo usan por debajo) datos que llegan de fuera
titulo.en: Unpickling data from outside (with pickle, or with joblib.load or torch.load, which use it underneath)

porque.es: Deserializar pickle puede ejecutar código arbitrario. La documentación de pickle lo advierte al menos desde Python 2.6 (2008) y hoy recomienda formatos más seguros como JSON para datos no confiables; joblib y PyTorch repiten el aviso para sus cargadores.
porque.en: Unpickling can execute arbitrary code. The pickle docs have warned about it since at least Python 2.6 (2008) and today recommend safer formats such as JSON for untrusted data; joblib and PyTorch repeat the warning for their loaders.

evidencia.cita: Never unpickle data received from an untrusted or unauthenticated source.
Oct 01 2008: Python 2.6 final released
It is possible to construct malicious pickle data which will execute arbitrary code during unpickling.
Safer serialization formats such as json may be more appropriate if you are processing untrusted data.
joblib.load relies on the pickle module and can therefore execute arbitrary Python code. It should therefore never be used to load files from untrusted sources.
torch.load() uses an unpickler under the hood. Never load data from an untrusted source.

nota.es: La documentación de Python 2.6 ya avisa: nunca deserializar datos no confiables.
nota.en: The Python 2.6 docs already warn: never unpickle untrusted data.

titulo.es: Pasar a unserialize() datos que llegan del usuario (cookies, formularios, peticiones)
titulo.en: Passing user-supplied data (cookies, forms, requests) to unserialize()

porque.es: Deserializar puede cargar y ejecutar código por la creación de objetos y la autocarga, y un atacante puede aprovecharlo. El manual lo prohíbe desde 2012, y desde 2016 aclara que allowed_classes no lo arregla; para intercambiar datos, JSON. Es la misma práctica que en Python (ver unpickle-de-datos-no-confiables).
porque.en: Unserializing can load and execute code through object instantiation and autoloading, and an attacker may exploit it. The manual has forbidden it since 2012, and since 2016 it says allowed_classes does not fix it; use JSON to exchange data. Same practice as in Python (see unpickle-de-datos-no-confiables).

evidencia.cita: Unserialization can result in code being loaded and executed due to object instantiation and autoloading, and a malicious user may be able to exploit this.
Do not pass untrusted user input to unserialize() regardless of the options value of allowed_classes.
Fix #73836: unserialize() with $options['allowed_classes'] = null behaves different

nota.es: El manual añade el aviso: no pasar entrada no fiable a unserialize(); usar JSON.
nota.en: The manual adds the warning: do not pass untrusted input to unserialize(); use JSON.

titulo.es: Declarar las variables de JavaScript con var

porque.es: var tiene ámbito de función, no de bloque. Desde ES2015 hay let y const, con ámbito de bloque (en los navegadores principales desde septiembre de 2016), y la guía de estilo de MDN pide usarlos. var no está deprecado en el estándar: lo superado es la práctica, no la sintaxis.
porque.en: var is function-scoped, not block-scoped. Since ES2015 there are let and const, block-scoped (in major browsers since September 2016), and MDN’s style guide asks to use them. var is not deprecated in the standard: the practice is superseded, not the syntax.

evidencia.cita: Some of its major enhancements include modules, class declarations, lexical block scoping, iterators and generators, promises for asynchronous programming, destructuring patterns, and proper tail calls.

evidencia.titulo: Guidelines for writing JavaScript code examples (MDN)
evidencia.cita: When declaring variables and constants, use the let and const keywords, not var.
It's been available across browsers since September 2016.

evidencia.titulo: MDN — JavaScript Guide: Values, variables, and literals (captura de Wayback Machine, 16-01-2014)
evidencia.cita: You can declare a variable in two ways: With the keyword var. For example, var x = 42. This syntax can be used to declare both local and global variables.

porque.es: ViewModel guarda en caché el estado de la pantalla y lo conserva a través de los cambios de configuración, así que la interfaz no tiene que volver a cargar los datos. Es lo que Google recomienda desde que deprecó los Loaders en Android 9 (ver loaders-en-android).
porque.en: ViewModel caches screen state and keeps it across configuration changes, so the UI does not have to reload data. It is what Google recommends since it deprecated Loaders in Android 9 (see loaders-en-android).

evidencia.cita: Its principal advantage is that it caches state and persists it through configuration changes.
The recommended option for dealing with loading data while handling the Activity and Fragment lifecycles is to use a combination of ViewModel objects and LiveData
Today we're pushing the source code to Android Open Source Project (AOSP), and starting the Android 9 rollout to all Pixel users worldwide
