titulo.es: Tomar el razonamiento visible del modelo (chain of thought, thinking) como explicación fiel o registro de auditoría de por qué decidió
titulo.en: Treating the model's visible reasoning (chain of thought, thinking) as a faithful explanation or audit log of why it decided

porque.es: El razonamiento escrito puede ser plausible y no reflejar la causa real de la respuesta. Con pistas ocultas en el prompt, Claude 3.7 Sonnet solo las mencionó el 25 % de las veces y DeepSeek R1 el 39 %; al hacer trampas, lo admitieron menos del 2 % de las veces.
porque.en: Written reasoning can be plausible yet not reflect the real cause of the answer. With hints hidden in the prompt, Claude 3.7 Sonnet mentioned them only 25% of the time and DeepSeek R1 39%; when exploiting reward hacks, they admitted it under 2% of the time.

evidencia.titulo: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting (Turpin et al., arXiv / NeurIPS 2023)
evidencia.cita: we find that CoT explanations can systematically misrepresent the true reason for a model's prediction.

evidencia.titulo: Reasoning models don't always say what they think (Anthropic)
evidencia.cita: On average across all the different hint types, Claude 3.7 Sonnet mentioned the hint 25% of the time, and DeepSeek R1 mentioned it 39% of the time.

evidencia.titulo: Reasoning models don't always say what they think (Anthropic)
evidencia.cita: The models very rarely admitted to using the reward hacks in their Chain-of-Thought explanations, doing so less than 2% of the time in most of the testing scenarios.

nota.es: Turpin et al.: las explicaciones chain of thought pueden justificar respuestas sesgadas sin mencionar el sesgo que las provocó (p. ej. reordenar las opciones para que la buena sea siempre la «(A)»).
nota.en: Turpin et al.: chain-of-thought explanations can justify biased answers without mentioning the bias that caused them (e.g. reordering options so the right one is always "(A)").

nota.es: Anthropic lo confirma en modelos de razonamiento: la mayoría de las cadenas de pensamiento omiten la pista que usaron, y casi nunca confiesan el «reward hacking».
nota.en: Anthropic confirms it on reasoning models: most chains of thought omit the hint they used and almost never admit reward hacking.

titulo.es: Reentrenar o ajustar un modelo, generación tras generación, con datos generados por modelos en vez de datos reales
titulo.en: Retraining or fine-tuning a model, generation after generation, on model-generated data instead of real data

porque.es: Entrenar generación tras generación con datos generados por modelos, sustituyendo a los reales, provoca «colapso del modelo»: desaparecen las colas de la distribución original y los defectos son irreversibles. En los experimentos de Gerstgrasser et al., acumular los datos sintéticos junto a los reales, en vez de sustituirlos, evitó el colapso.
porque.en: Training generation after generation on model-generated data that replaces real data causes model collapse: the tails of the original distribution vanish and the defects are irreversible. In Gerstgrasser et al.'s experiments, accumulating synthetic data alongside real data, instead of replacing it, avoided collapse.

evidencia.titulo: The Curse of Recursion: Training on Generated Data Makes Models Forget (Shumailov et al., arXiv)
evidencia.cita: We find that use of model-generated content in training causes irreversible defects in the resulting models, where tails of the original content distribution disappear.

evidencia.titulo: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data (Shumailov et al., Nature)
evidencia.cita: We find that indiscriminate use of model-generated content in training causes irreversible defects in the resulting models, in which tails of the original content distribution disappear.

evidencia.titulo: Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data (Gerstgrasser et al., arXiv)
evidencia.cita: We confirm that replacing the original real data by each generation's synthetic data does indeed tend towards model collapse, then demonstrate that accumulating the successive generations of synthetic data alongside the original real data avoids model collapse

nota.es: Shumailov et al. (preprint «The Curse of Recursion») describen el colapso del modelo en LLM, VAE y GMM.
nota.en: Shumailov et al. (preprint "The Curse of Recursion") describe model collapse in LLMs, VAEs and GMMs.

nota.es: Gerstgrasser et al. (preprint) confirman el colapso al sustituir los datos reales y muestran que acumularlos junto a los sintéticos lo evita.
nota.en: Gerstgrasser et al. (preprint) confirm collapse when real data is replaced and show that accumulating it alongside synthetic data avoids it.

titulo.es: Ejecutar en el hilo principal una expresión regular que escribe el usuario, sin límite de tiempo
titulo.en: Running a user-written regular expression on the main thread with no time limit

porque.es: Un patrón con backtracking catastrófico, como (a+)+$, tarda el doble por cada carácter que no casa: no es lentitud, es un cuelgue. Ni un setTimeout ni un try/catch lo cortan; solo sacarlo a un Worker que se pueda terminar.
porque.en: A pattern with catastrophic backtracking, such as (a+)+$, doubles its time with every non-matching character: it is a hang, not slowness. Neither setTimeout nor try/catch stops it; only running it in a Worker that can be terminated.

porque.es: El fichero de contexto es un consejo para el modelo, no una regla que se haga cumplir: puede ignorarlo, y es de las quejas más repetidas. Lo que tiene que pasar siempre, o no pasar nunca, va en hooks o en reglas de permisos, que ejecuta el cliente (ver agents-md-y-claude-md-en-el-repositorio).
porque.en: The context file is advice to the model, not an enforced rule: it can ignore it, and that is one of the most repeated complaints. What must always (or never) happen belongs in hooks or permission rules, which the client enforces (see agents-md-y-claude-md-en-el-repositorio).

porque.es: Si las respuestas no coinciden, es una señal de alucinación, y votar suele mejorar la precisión en problemas con una respuesta clara. Pero multiplica el coste y la latencia por N, así que solo compensa en decisiones donde un error sale caro.
porque.en: If the answers disagree, that signals a hallucination, and voting usually improves accuracy on problems with a clear answer. But it multiplies cost and latency by N, so it only pays off where a mistake is expensive.

cuando.en: long free text or high volume

titulo.es: Resumir un documento largo por trozos y luego resumir los resúmenes (map-reduce)
titulo.en: Summarizing a long document in chunks and then summarizing the summaries (map-reduce)

porque.es: El map-reduce sirve cuando el texto es largo comparado con la ventana del modelo, y funciona mejor cuando cada trozo se entiende sin lo anterior (muchos documentos cortos); en un texto con hilo continuo, como una novela, LangChain propone el refinado iterativo. Si el documento cabe, una sola llamada lo conserva, aunque con mucho contexto la precisión baja («context rot»). Es el caso de resumen de trocear un documento que no cabe (ver trocear-documento-por-limite-de-ventana).
porque.en: Map-reduce helps when the text is long compared to the model's window, and works best when each chunk can be understood without what came before (many short documents); for a text with a continuous thread, like a novel, LangChain suggests iterative refinement. If the document fits, a single call keeps it, although accuracy drops with a lot of context ("context rot"). It is the summarization case of chunking a document that does not fit (see trocear-documento-por-limite-de-ventana).

cuando.es: el documento cabe holgadamente en la ventana y tiene un hilo continuo (un informe, un libro, un contrato)
cuando.en: the document fits comfortably in the window and has a continuous thread (a report, a book, a contract)

porque.es: Una sola llamada («stuff») conserva el contexto entre partes; LangChain la propone con modelos de ventana grande.
porque.en: A single call ("stuff") keeps the context across parts; LangChain suggests it with large-window models.

cuando.es: el corpus no cabe, o son muchos documentos cortos e independientes
cuando.en: the corpus does not fit, or there are many short independent documents

porque.es: Cada trozo se entiende por separado, o el texto no cabe en la ventana.
porque.en: Each chunk stands on its own, or the text does not fit in the window.

evidencia.cita: Note that map-reduce is especially effective when understanding of a sub-document does not rely on preceding context. For example, when summarizing a corpus of many, shorter documents. In other cases, such as summarizing a novel or body of text with an inherent sequence, [iterative refinement](/docs/how_to/summarize_refine) may be more effective.
Map-reduce flows are particularly useful when texts are long compared to the context window of a LLM.
especially if using larger context window models such as:
As token count grows, accuracy and recall degrade, a phenomenon known as context rot.

OpenAI cuenta que Cursor vio que partes de su prompt que funcionaban con modelos anteriores había que ajustarlas para GPT-5, y Anthropic pide en su guía de migración revisar las instrucciones pensadas para el modelo anterior. Cambiar de modelo es cambiar de prompt: hay que pasar las evals otra vez (ver evaluar-con-un-conjunto-de-evals).
porque.en: Each model reacts differently to the same text. OpenAI reports that Cursor found parts of its prompt that worked with older models needed tuning for GPT-5, and Anthropic's migration guide asks you to review instructions tuned for the previous model. Switching models means switching prompts: rerun your evals (see evaluar-con-un-conjunto-de-evals).

evidencia.cita: While this worked well with older models that needed encouragement to analyze context thoroughly, they found it counterproductive with GPT-5, which is already naturally introspective and proactive at gathering context.

We've launched Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), a model for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work.

porque.es: La API restringe la generación al esquema, así que la respuesta lo cumple salvo rechazo o corte por longitud. porque.es: Sirve para probar y comparar modelos cambiando solo la URL. porque.en: It is handy for trying and comparing models by changing only the URL. But Anthropic says its compatible layer is not a production solution: it silently ignores many parameters, does not guarantee tool schemas and offers no prompt caching or thinking output. Google's is still in beta and, if you are not already using the OpenAI libraries, it recommends calling the Gemini API directly.

titulo.es: Guardar secretos (claves, credenciales, reglas de acceso) en el prompt de sistema confiando en que el modelo no los revele
titulo.en: Keeping secrets (keys, credentials, access rules) in the system prompt trusting the model not to reveal them

porque.es: El prompt de sistema se puede extraer: no es un secreto ni un control de seguridad. OWASP lo añadió como riesgo propio en su lista de 2025 por incidentes reales, y en la de 2026 lo amplía a todo el contexto oculto.
porque.en: The system prompt can be extracted: it is neither a secret nor a security control. OWASP added it as its own risk in the 2025 list because of real incidents, and the 2026 list widens it to all hidden context.

evidencia.titulo: LLM07:2025 System Prompt Leakage (OWASP; fecha de la versión 2025 de la lista)
evidencia.cita: It's important to understand that the system prompt should not be considered a secret, nor should it be used as a security control. Accordingly, sensitive data such as credentials, connection strings, etc. should not be contained within the system prompt language.
Many applications assumed prompts were securely isolated, but recent incidents have shown that developers cannot safely assume that information in these prompts remains secret.

evidencia.titulo: OWASP GenAI/LLM Top 10 2026 (PDF; la portada aún dice «Publication date to be set»)
evidencia.cita: Practitioners should design under the assumption that hidden context is discoverable and that any contents of the context should not be considered a secret.

titulo.es: Instalar servidores MCP de terceros sin revisar qué ejecutan ni fijar la versión (npx paquete@latest en la configuración)
titulo.en: Installing third-party MCP servers without reviewing what they run or pinning the version (npx package@latest in the config)

porque.es: Un servidor MCP local ejecuta código con tus permisos, y su descripción de herramientas entra en el prompt. Invariant Labs mostró envenenamiento de herramientas y un «rug pull» que cambia la herramienta a maliciosa en la segunda carga, y recomienda fijar versiones. Las buenas prácticas de seguridad de MCP exigen (MUST) a los clientes que permiten instalar con un clic mostrar el comando exacto y pedir consentimiento. Es el mismo problema que instalar-paquetes-que-sugiere-un-llm-sin-mirar, y se agrava sin sandbox (ver agente-de-codigo-sin-permisos-ni-sandbox).
porque.en: A local MCP server runs code with your permissions, and its tool descriptions go into the prompt. Invariant Labs showed tool poisoning and a rug pull that switches the tool to a malicious one on the second load, and recommends pinning versions. MCP security best practices require (MUST) clients that offer one-click install to show the exact command and ask for consent. Same problem as instalar-paquetes-que-sugiere-un-llm-sin-mirar, and worse without a sandbox (see agente-de-codigo-sin-permisos-ni-sandbox).

evidencia.titulo: MCP Tool Poisoning Experiments (Invariant Labs, README)
evidencia.cita: we implement a simple MCP server that instructs an agent to leak sensitive files, when calling the `add` tool (in this case SSH keys and the `mcp.json` file itself).

evidencia.titulo: MCP Tool Poisoning Experiments (Invariant Labs, README)
evidencia.cita: we implement a shadowing attack combined with a sleeper rug pull, i.e. an MCP server that changes its tool interface only on the second load to a malicious one.
Local MCP servers are binaries that are downloaded and executed on the same machine as the MCP client.
Show the exact command that will be executed, without truncation (include arguments and parameters)

evidencia.titulo: MCP Security Notification: Tool Poisoning Attacks (Invariant Labs)
evidencia.cita: Clients should pin the version of the MCP server and its tools to prevent unauthorized changes.
Local MCP servers are binaries that are downloaded and executed on the same machine as the MCP client.
Show the exact command that will be executed, without truncation (include arguments and parameters)

nota.es: Invariant Labs publica ataques de envenenamiento de herramientas, shadowing y rug pull con servidores MCP, y recomienda fijar la versión del servidor y de sus herramientas.
nota.en: Invariant Labs publishes tool poisoning, shadowing and rug pull attacks with MCP servers, and recommends pinning the version of the server and its tools.

titulo.es: Usar una sola sesión larga del agente de código para tareas distintas, corrigiéndolo una y otra vez en vez de empezar de cero
titulo.en: Using one long coding-agent session for unrelated tasks, correcting it again and again instead of starting fresh

porque.es: El contexto viejo gasta tokens en cada mensaje siguiente y el modelo rinde peor cuanto más lleno está. Anthropic lo señala como causa habitual de gasto inesperado: hay que limpiar (/clear) entre tareas distintas y, tras más de dos correcciones sobre lo mismo, empezar de nuevo con un prompt mejor. Es la cara de usuario de gestionar-el-contexto-en-agentes-largos (ver gestionar-el-contexto-en-agentes-largos).
porque.en: Stale context costs tokens on every later message, and the model does worse as the context fills. Anthropic names it a usual cause of unexpected spend: clear (/clear) between unrelated tasks and, after more than two corrections on the same issue, restart with a better prompt. It is the user-side face of gestionar-el-contexto-en-agentes-largos (see gestionar-el-contexto-en-agentes-largos).

evidencia.cita: usually traces back to long sessions that were never cleared or to Opus left as the default model.
Stale context wastes tokens on every subsequent message.

evidencia.titulo: Best practices for Claude Code (Claude Code docs)

evidencia.titulo: Best practices for Claude Code (Claude Code docs)
evidencia.cita: The kitchen sink session. You start with one task, then ask Claude something unrelated, then go back to the first task. Context is full of irrelevant information.

evidencia.titulo: Best practices for Claude Code (Claude Code docs)
evidencia.cita: If you've corrected Claude more than twice on the same issue in one session, the context is cluttered with failed approaches.

evidencia.titulo: Best practices for Claude Code (Claude Code docs)
evidencia.cita: A clean session with a better prompt almost always outperforms a long session with accumulated corrections.

nota.es: La documentación de Claude Code lo lista entre los fallos típicos («kitchen sink session»), lo da como causa habitual de gasto inesperado y aconseja /clear tras dos correcciones. Documentado así a fecha de revisión.
nota.en: Claude Code's docs list it among common failure patterns ("kitchen sink session"), name it a usual cause of unexpected spend and advise /clear after two corrections. Documented as such at review date.

titulo.es: Copiar un tamaño de trozo «estándar» para RAG (512 tokens con un 10–20 % de solapamiento) y no medirlo con tus datos
titulo.en: Copying a "standard" RAG chunk size (512 tokens with 10–20% overlap) without measuring it on your data

porque.es: No hay un número universal: Azure AI Search recomienda empezar con 512 tokens y un 25 % de solapamiento, LlamaIndex trae por defecto trozos de 1024 con 20 de solapamiento, y los dos dicen que hay que ajustarlo a tus datos. Anthropic avisa de que el tamaño, las fronteras y el solapamiento cambian la recuperación. Sirve como punto de partida, no como ajuste final (ver rag-solo-con-busqueda-vectorial).
porque.en: There is no universal number: Azure AI Search recommends starting with 512 tokens and 25% overlap, LlamaIndex defaults to chunks of 1024 with 20 overlap, and both say to tune it to your data. Anthropic warns that chunk size, boundaries and overlap change retrieval. Fine as a starting point, not as a final setting (see rag-solo-con-busqueda-vectorial).

porque.es: El tamaño adecuado depende del contenido y de las consultas; sin evals de recuperación no se sabe si el elegido funciona.
porque.en: The right size depends on the content and the queries; without retrieval evals you can't tell whether the chosen one works.

titulo.es: Fijar temperature a 0 creyendo que así las respuestas son idénticas y reproducibles
titulo.en: Setting temperature to 0 believing it makes responses identical and reproducible

porque.es: Anthropic avisa de que ni con temperatura 0 la salida es del todo determinista, y OpenAI de que puede variar aun con los mismos parámetros y seed, que es solo «best effort». Y desde Claude Opus 4.7 (abril de 2026), fijar una temperatura distinta de 1 en los modelos nuevos de Anthropic devuelve un error 400: para fijar el comportamiento, el prompt.
porque.en: Anthropic warns output is not fully deterministic even at temperature 0, and OpenAI that it can vary even with the same parameters and seed, which is only "best effort". And since Claude Opus 4.7 (April 2026), setting a temperature other than 1 on new Anthropic models returns a 400 error: use the prompt to steer behaviour.

titulo.es: Validar con tests de mutación los tests que escribe la IA, en vez de fiarse del porcentaje de cobertura
titulo.en: Validating AI-written tests with mutation testing instead of trusting the coverage percentage

porque.es: Una cobertura alta puede esconder tests que siempre pasan (sin asserts o con mocks desacoplados), muy comunes cuando los genera la IA. Los tests de mutación meten fallos a propósito y comprueban que algún test se rompe; sobre todo en la lógica de dominio central.
porque.en: High coverage can hide always-green tests (no asserts, decoupled mocks), common when AI writes them. Mutation testing injects deliberate bugs and checks that some test breaks, particularly in core domain logic.

evidencia.titulo: Thoughtworks Technology Radar Vol. 34 — Mutation testing (Trial)
evidencia.cita: This distinction is critical in an era of AI-assisted development, where high coverage percentages can mask logically hollow tests or generated code that has never been meaningfully asserted.

evidencia.titulo: Thoughtworks Technology Radar Vol. 34 — Mutation testing (Trial)
evidencia.cita: By using tools such as Stryker, Pitest or cargo-mutants, we shift the focus from how much code is executed to how much code is actually verified, particularly in core domain logic.

porque.en: Claude’s window went from 9,000 to 100,000 tokens in 2023 and Gemini opened 2 million to everyone in 2024, so it often fits now. titulo.es: Poner alertas que despiertan por causas (CPU alta, un proceso caído…) en lugar de por síntomas que nota el usuario
titulo.en: Paging on causes (high CPU, a process down…) instead of on symptoms users notice

porque.es: Las alertas por causas dan ruido y páginas sin nada que hacer. Prometheus recomienda desde 2015 tener pocas alertas, por síntomas ligados al dolor del usuario (latencia, errores), y usar paneles para encontrar la causa; el libro SRE de Google pide avisar a una persona solo cuando el problema ya está causando síntomas reales. Excepción explícita: avisar cuando se está cerca del límite de capacidad (p. ej. disco), porque necesita intervención antes de la caída.
porque.en: Cause-based alerts produce noise and pages with nothing to do. Since 2015 Prometheus recommends few alerts, on symptoms tied to user pain (latency, errors), with dashboards to find the cause; Google's SRE book asks to page a human only when the problem is already causing real symptoms. Explicit exception: alerting when close to capacity (e.g. disk), because it needs intervention before an outage.

evidencia.cita: To summarize, keep alerting simple, alert on symptoms, have good consoles to allow pinpointing causes and avoid having pages where there is nothing to do.
Aim to have as few alerts as possible, by alerting on symptoms that are associated with end-user pain rather than trying to catch every possible way that pain could be caused.

evidencia.titulo: Monitoring Distributed Systems (Site Reliability Engineering, Google)
evidencia.cita: For paging, black-box monitoring has the key benefit of forcing discipline to only nag a human when a problem is both already ongoing and contributing to real symptoms.
While not a problem causing immediate user impact, being close to capacity often requires human intervention to avoid an outage in the near future.

titulo.es: Aprobar o bloquear un cambio en el CI con una sola ejecución de cada caso de eval del LLM o del agente
titulo.en: Passing or blocking a change in CI with a single run of each LLM or agent eval case

porque.es: La salida del modelo cambia entre ejecuciones: un caso que pasa hoy puede fallar mañana sin tocar nada, y la puerta se vuelve aleatoria. τ-bench (Sierra, junio de 2024) propone pass^k para medir la fiabilidad repitiendo cada tarea, y Anthropic (2024 y 2026) pide varias respuestas o pruebas por tarea. La alternativa: ver repetir-pruebas-y-medir-pass-k; es la versión de CI de evaluar-un-prompt-con-un-solo-formato.
porque.en: Model output varies between runs: a case that passes today can fail tomorrow with nothing changed, and the gate becomes random. τ-bench (Sierra, June 2024) proposes pass^k to measure reliability by repeating each task, and Anthropic (2024 and 2026) asks for several answers or trials per task. The alternative: see repetir-pruebas-y-medir-pass-k; this is the CI version of evaluar-un-prompt-con-un-solo-formato.

titulo.es: Emitir certificados TLS públicos que duren más de un año
titulo.en: Issuing public TLS certificates valid for more than a year

porque.es: La vida máxima de un certificado público bajó de 39 meses a 825 días (2018) y a 398 (2020: lo impuso Apple y el CA/B Forum lo adoptó en julio de 2020, después de que en 2019 fracasara una votación para bajar a un año). Desde el 15 de marzo de 2026 es de 200 días, y está aprobado bajar a 100 en 2027 y a 47 en 2029.
porque.en: The maximum lifetime of a public certificate dropped from 39 months to 825 days (2018) and to 398 (2020: Apple imposed it and the CA/B Forum adopted it in July 2020, after a 2019 vote to cut to one year failed). Since 15 March 2026 it is 200 days, with 100 approved for 2027 and 47 for 2029.

evidencia.cita: Recent Ballot 185 demonstrated a consensus among Forum members to reduce the maximum lifetime for DV and OV certificates from 39 months to 825 days (roughly 27 months).

porque.es: Con la lista desactivada, un job de cualquier otro proyecto puede usar su token para acceder al tuyo; GitLab lo llama riesgo de seguridad, porque un usuario malicioso podría comprometer un pipeline de un proyecto no autorizado y usar el token. Desde GitLab 15.9 (febrero de 2023) los proyectos nuevos traen la lista activada, y GitLab anunció que la 18.0 la impondría por defecto en todas las instancias.
porque.en: With the allowlist off, a job from any other project can use its token to access yours; GitLab calls this a security risk, because a malicious user could compromise a pipeline in an unauthorized project and use the token. Since GitLab 15.9 (February 2023) new projects have the allowlist on, and GitLab announced that 18.0 would enforce it by default on all instances.

porque.es: Las instancias de `count` se identifican por posición: si quitas un elemento del medio de la lista, todas las siguientes cambian y Terraform las modifica o recrea. Desde Terraform 0.12.6 (julio de 2019) `for_each` las identifica por clave estable.
porque.en: `count` instances are identified by position: remove an element from the middle of the list and every later one shifts, so Terraform modifies or recreates them. Since Terraform 0.12.6 (July 2019) `for_each` identifies them by a stable key.

evidencia.cita: When declaring multiple instances of a resource using [`count`](#count), it is common to want each instance to have a different value for a given attribute.
config: Resources can now use a for_each meta-argument

This means that if an element is removed from the middle of the list, all of the indexed instances _after_ it will see their `subnet_id` values change, which will cause more remote object changes than were probably intended.

Use the `count` argument when you want to create nearly identical instances. Use `for_each` when some instance arguments must have distinct values that can't be directly derived from an integer index.

nota.es: En Terraform 0.11 `count` con `count.index` es la única forma de crear varias instancias con valores distintos.
nota.en: In Terraform 0.11 `count` with `count.index` is the only way to create several instances with different values.

nota.es: Terraform 0.12.6 añade `for_each` a los recursos; su documentación avisa del desplazamiento de índices al usar listas con `count`. La guía actual reserva `count` para instancias casi idénticas.
nota.en: Terraform 0.12.6 adds `for_each` to resources; its docs warn about index shifting when using lists with `count`. Current guidance keeps `count` for nearly identical instances.

porque.en: Since February 2024 Gmail has required senders of more than 5,000 messages a day to have SPF, DKIM, DMARC (`p=none` is enough) and one-click unsubscribe, and Yahoo requires the same of bulk senders (with RFC 8058 strongly recommended); since November 2025 Gmail temporarily or permanently rejects non-compliant mail. Outlook.com announced in April 2025 that it would require SPF, DKIM and DMARC from May and reject mail that fails them.

porque.es: El estado guarda los atributos de los recursos, y en bases de datos puede incluir contraseñas iniciales; el estado local es JSON en texto plano. Desde Terraform 0.9 (marzo de 2017) hay backends remotos con bloqueo, y HashiCorp pide no guardarlo en un control de versiones ni en un almacén sin bloqueo ni control de acceso, por riesgo de pérdida de datos o de exponer secretos.
porque.en: State stores resource attributes, and for databases it may include initial passwords; local state is plain-text JSON. Since Terraform 0.9 (March 2017) there are remote backends with locking, and HashiCorp says not to keep it in version control or in storage without locking and access control, because of data loss or exposure of secrets.

evidencia.cita: Backends supporting locking in this release are Local, S3 (via DynamoDB), and Consul.
When using local state, state is stored in plain-text JSON files.
For resources such as databases, this may contain initial passwords.

Avoid storing your state in a version control system or other storage solution that does not support Terraform state locking and secure access control, because doing so can result in data loss or exposure of secrets stored in the state file.
S3 native state locking is now generally available. The `use_lockfile` argument enables users to adopt the S3-native mechanism for state locking.

nota.es: Terraform 0.9.0 introduce los backends y el bloqueo automático del estado (local, S3 con DynamoDB, Consul). La documentación de la época avisa de que el estado local es JSON en texto plano.
nota.en: Terraform 0.9.0 introduces backends and automatic state locking (local, S3 via DynamoDB, Consul). The docs of the time warn that local state is plain-text JSON.

nota.es: Terraform 1.11.0: el bloqueo nativo en S3 (`use_lockfile`) pasa a estable; ya no hace falta ni una tabla DynamoDB para tener backend remoto con bloqueo. La guía actual dice que no se guarde el estado en un control de versiones.
nota.en: Terraform 1.11.0: native S3 locking (`use_lockfile`) becomes GA; a remote backend with locking no longer even needs a DynamoDB table. Current docs say not to keep state in version control.

La guía de Prometheus lo desaconseja expresamente desde diciembre de 2014 (IDs de usuario, emails y otros conjuntos sin límite) y recomienda que la gran mayoría de las métricas no tengan etiquetas.
porque.en: Every distinct combination of label values is a new time series, which can greatly increase the data stored. Prometheus's guide has explicitly advised against it since December 2014 (user IDs, email addresses and other unbounded sets) and recommends that the vast majority of metrics have no labels.

The vast majority of your metrics should have no labels.

titulo.es: Exigir IMDSv2 en las instancias EC2 (`HttpTokens=required`)

porque.es: El token de sesión de IMDSv2 corta el robo de credenciales por SSRF, cortafuegos abiertos y proxies inversos. Por defecto una instancia sigue aceptando v1 y v2, así que hay que exigirlo: por instancia (2019), por AMI (2022) o con los valores por defecto de la cuenta (2024).
porque.en: IMDSv2's session token stops credential theft through SSRF, open firewalls and reverse proxies. By default an instance still accepts both v1 and v2, so it has to be required: per instance (2019), per AMI (2022) or through account defaults (2024).

porque.es: Con IMDSv1 basta un SSRF, un cortafuegos abierto o un proxy inverso mal configurado para leer las credenciales del rol de la instancia. IMDSv2 (noviembre de 2019) exige un token de sesión y AWS recomienda restringir la instancia a v2; desde 2024 se puede imponer por defecto en toda la cuenta (ver exigir-imdsv2-en-ec2).
porque.en: With IMDSv1, an SSRF, an open firewall or a misconfigured reverse proxy is enough to read the instance role's credentials. IMDSv2 (November 2019) requires a session token and AWS recommends restricting instances to v2; since 2024 it can be enforced by default across the account (see exigir-imdsv2-en-ec2).

titulo.es: Usar el nuevo protocolo de rebalanceo del consumidor de Kafka (group.protocol=consumer)
titulo.en: Using the new Kafka consumer rebalance protocol (group.protocol=consumer)

porque.es: KIP-848 es GA desde Kafka 4.0 (marzo de 2025): los rebalanceos son totalmente incrementales, sin barrera de sincronización global. En el servidor está activo por defecto, pero el KafkaConsumer sigue usando el protocolo clásico hasta que se pone group.protocol=consumer. Kafka 4.3 (mayo de 2026) avisa en el log al usar el clásico, y KIP-1274 prevé que consumer sea el valor por defecto en Kafka 5.0 y el único en 6.0.
porque.en: KIP-848 is GA since Kafka 4.0 (March 2025): rebalances are fully incremental, with no global synchronization barrier. It is enabled by default on the server, but KafkaConsumer keeps using the classic protocol until group.protocol=consumer is set. Kafka 4.3 (May 2026) logs a message when the classic one is used, and KIP-1274 plans consumer as the default in Kafka 5.0 and the only option in 6.0.

evidencia.cita: The new protocol is enabled by default on the server side. Consumers must opt-in by setting group.protocol=consumer.
However, the protocol is not enabled by default. The group.protocol configuration must be set to consumer to enable it.
Starting from Apache Kafka 4.0, the Next Generation of the Consumer Rebalance Protocol (KIP-848) is Generally Available (GA), ready for production workloads.

Logs a message when starting a consumer with the classic rebalance protocol recommending to use the new consumer rebalance protocol instead as the classic protocol will be deprecated in a future release.

nota.en: Kafka 4.3 starts recommending the new protocol in the classic consumer log; the client still does not enable it by default.

titulo.es: Desplegar Kafka en modo KRaft (sin ZooKeeper)
titulo.en: Running Kafka in KRaft mode (no ZooKeeper)

porque.es: KRaft guarda los metadatos en el propio Kafka, sin un ensemble de ZooKeeper aparte. Es apto para producción en clústeres nuevos desde Kafka 3.3 (octubre de 2022) y es el único modo desde Kafka 4.0 (marzo de 2025) (ver kafka-con-zookeeper).
porque.en: KRaft keeps metadata inside Kafka itself, with no separate ZooKeeper ensemble. It has been production ready for new clusters since Kafka 3.3 (October 2022) and is the only mode since Kafka 4.0 (March 2025) (see kafka-con-zookeeper).

evidencia.cita: KRaft mode is production ready for new clusters.
By running in KRaft mode by default, Kafka simplifies deployment and management, eliminating the complexity of maintaining a separate ZooKeeper ensemble.
Note: Apache Kafka 4.0 only supports KRaft mode - ZooKeeper mode has been removed.

nota.es: Kafka 3.3.1 declara KRaft apto para producción en clústeres nuevos.
nota.en: Kafka 3.3.1 declares KRaft production ready for new clusters.

nota.es: Kafka 4.0: KRaft pasa a ser el único modo.
nota.en: Kafka 4.0: KRaft becomes the only mode.

titulo.es: Poner a mano enable.idempotence=true y acks=all en el productor de Kafka
titulo.en: Manually setting enable.idempotence=true and acks=all on the Kafka producer

porque.es: Desde Kafka 3.0 (septiembre de 2021) el productor de Apache Kafka usa por defecto acks=all e idempotencia (KIP-679), siempre que no haya otra configuración que la contradiga. Un fallo impedía aplicar la idempotencia en 3.0.0 y 3.1.0; está corregido desde 3.0.1, 3.1.1 y 3.2.0. Kafka Connect es la excepción: desactiva la idempotencia en sus productores salvo que se configure.
porque.en: Since Kafka 3.0 (September 2021) the Apache Kafka producer uses acks=all and idempotence by default (KIP-679), as long as no conflicting configuration is set. A bug prevented idempotence from being applied in 3.0.0 and 3.1.0; it is fixed since 3.0.1, 3.1.1 and 3.2.0. Kafka Connect is the exception: it disables idempotence for its producers unless configured.

evidencia.cita: The producer has stronger delivery guarantees by default: idempotence is enabled and acks is set to all instead of 1.
This issue was fixed and the default is properly applied in 3.0.1, 3.1.1, and 3.2.0.
A notable exception is Connect that by default disables idempotent behavior for all of its producers in order to uniformly support using a wide range of Kafka broker versions.
Idempotence for the producer is enabled by default if no conflicting configurations are set.

nota.es: Kafka 3.0 cambia los valores por defecto del productor a idempotencia y acks=all (KIP-679), aunque un fallo impedía aplicar la idempotencia en 3.0.0 y 3.1.0.
nota.en: Kafka 3.0 changes the producer defaults to idempotence and acks=all (KIP-679), although a bug prevented idempotence from being applied in 3.0.0 and 3.1.0.

nota.es: Kafka 3.2.0 (y 3.0.1, 3.1.1) aplica de verdad la idempotencia por defecto si no hay configuraciones que la contradigan. Connect sigue desactivándola salvo que se configure.
nota.en: Kafka 3.2.0 (and 3.0.1, 3.1.1) really applies idempotence by default when no conflicting configuration is set. Connect still disables it unless configured.

porque.es: Los ficheros se pierden con el contenedor y `docker logs` o `kubectl logs` no los ven: lo que la plataforma recoge es stdout y stderr (ver logs-a-stdout-y-stderr). Twelve-Factor (2011) ya pedía no gestionar ficheros de log.
porque.en: The files are lost with the container and `docker logs` or `kubectl logs` cannot see them: what the platform collects is stdout and stderr (see logs-a-stdout-y-stderr). Twelve-Factor (2011) already said not to manage logfiles.

evidencia.cita: It should not attempt to write to or manage logfiles.
that application may send its output to log files instead of `STDOUT` and `STDERR`.

titulo.es: Usar proveedores de Terraform sin restricción de versión y sin subir `.terraform.lock.hcl`

porque.es: Sin `version` Terraform acepta cualquier versión del proveedor como compatible. Desde Terraform 0.14 (diciembre de 2020) `terraform init` genera `.terraform.lock.hcl` para repetir las mismas versiones, y HashiCorp recomienda «encarecidamente» restringir la versión de cada proveedor y versionar ese fichero (ver fijar-proveedores-terraform-y-lock-hcl).
porque.en: Without `version` Terraform accepts any provider version as compatible. Since Terraform 0.14 (December 2020) `terraform init` writes `.terraform.lock.hcl` so the same versions are selected again, and HashiCorp "strongly recommends" a version constraint for every provider and committing that file (see fijar-proveedores-terraform-y-lock-hcl).

evidencia.cita: `terraform init` will now generate a lock file in the configuration directory which you can check in to your version control so that Terraform can make the same version selections in future.

The `version` argument is optional; if omitted, Terraform will accept any version of the provider as compatible. However, we strongly recommend specifying a version constraint for every provider your module depends on.
You should include this file in your version control repository so that you can discuss potential changes to your external dependencies via code review

nota.en: Terraform 0.14.0 generates the dependency lock file to be checked into version control. Current docs "strongly recommend" constraining every provider version and committing that file.

porque.es: Las colas quorum llegaron con RabbitMQ 3.8 (octubre de 2019) sobre Raft. La documentación las presenta como la opción por defecto cuando se necesita una cola replicada y de alta disponibilidad, y desde RabbitMQ 4.0 (septiembre de 2024) son, con los streams, los tipos replicados que quedan (ver rabbitmq-colas-clasicas-espejadas).
porque.en: Quorum queues arrived with RabbitMQ 3.8 (October 2019), built on Raft. The docs present them as the default choice when a replicated, highly available queue is needed, and since RabbitMQ 4.0 (September 2024) they are, together with streams, the replicated types that remain (see rabbitmq-colas-clasicas-espejadas).

evidencia.cita: built on top of the [Raft consensus algorithm](https://raft.github.io/) for data safety,
[Quorum queues](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/quorum-queues) and [streams](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/streams) are two mature replicated data types offered by RabbitMQ 4.x.

The RabbitMQ quorum queue is a modern queue type which implements a durable, replicated queue based on the Raft consensus algorithm and should be considered the default choice when needing a replicated, highly available queue.
Customers should make use of Quorum Queues for replication and data safety.

This document describes a protocol that a CA and an applicant can use to automate the process of verification and certificate issuance.

titulo.es: Emitir y renovar a mano los certificados TLS públicos

porque.es: Con vidas cada vez más cortas (200 días como máximo desde marzo de 2026, y 47 previstos para 2029), renovar a mano no escala. ACME es el estándar para automatizarlo desde 2019, y Let's Encrypt desaconseja expresamente renovar a mano.
porque.en: With ever shorter lifetimes (200 days at most since March 2026, 47 planned for 2029), manual renewal does not scale. ACME has been the standard for automating it since 2019, and Let's Encrypt explicitly advises against manual renewal.

evidencia.titulo: Why ninety-day lifetimes for certificates? (Let's Encrypt)
evidencia.cita: If we're going to move the entire Web to HTTPS, we can't continue to expect system administrators to manually handle renewals.
Furthermore, the maintenance of that CA-issued certificate would require minimal manual intervention.

titulo.es: Repetir cada tarea de eval varias veces y medir pass@k o pass^k, con su error estándar
titulo.en: Repeating each eval task several times and measuring pass@k or pass^k, with its standard error

porque.es: pass@k (al menos un acierto en k) sirve si basta con que una salga bien; pass^k (las k bien) mide la fiabilidad que espera un usuario: con un 75 % por prueba, 3 de 3 baja al 42 %. Anthropic pide además dar el error estándar (intervalo del 95 % = media ± 1,96 × SEM). Ojo con la caché de respuestas en CI: en promptfoo hay que usar --no-cache con --repeat para hacer llamadas nuevas.
porque.en: pass@k (at least one success in k) fits when one good answer is enough; pass^k (all k succeed) measures the reliability a user expects: at 75% per trial, 3 out of 3 drops to 42%. Anthropic also asks for the standard error (95% interval = mean ± 1.96 × SEM). Beware response caches in CI: in promptfoo use --no-cache with --repeat to make fresh calls.

evidencia.cita: We also propose a new metric (pass^k) to evaluate the reliability of agent behavior over multiple trials.

evidencia.titulo: A statistical approach to model evaluations (Anthropic)
evidencia.cita: A 95% confidence interval can be calculated from the SEM by adding and subtracting 1.96 ×

evidencia.titulo: Demystifying evals for AI agents (Anthropic Engineering)
evidencia.cita: pass^k measures the probability that all k trials succeed. As k increases, pass^k falls since demanding consistency across more trials is a harder bar to clear.

evidencia.titulo: Demystifying evals for AI agents (Anthropic Engineering)
evidencia.cita: pass@k for tools where one success matters, pass^k for agents where consistency is essential.
Use `--no-cache` with `--repeat` when you want every run to make fresh LLM calls instead of replaying each repeat index from cache.

nota.en: The τ-bench paper proposes the pass^k metric (all k trials succeed) to measure an agent’s reliability.

nota.es: Anthropic recomienda dar el error estándar y el intervalo de confianza junto a cada nota de eval, y reducir la varianza generando varias respuestas por pregunta.

titulo.es: Pasar en cada pull request un revisor de IA con contexto de todo el repositorio y hallazgos verificados, que deja comentarios y un check no bloqueante (no una aprobación)
titulo.en: Running on every pull request an AI reviewer with whole-repository context and verified findings, which leaves comments and a non-blocking check (not an approval)

porque.es: Los revisores de IA de 2026 ya no miran solo el diff: recogen contexto del repositorio con herramientas, verifican cada hallazgo para quitar falsos positivos y lo ordenan por gravedad. Anthropic cuenta que en sus PR los que reciben comentarios sustanciales pasaron del 16 % al 54 %. Su resultado es un comentario o un check que no bloquea, no una aprobación: la aprobación sigue siendo humana (ver revision-de-ia-como-complemento-de-la-humana).
porque.en: 2026 AI reviewers no longer look only at the diff: they gather repository context with tools, verify each finding to filter false positives and rank them by severity. Anthropic reports that PRs receiving substantive comments went from 16% to 54% internally. Their output is a comment or a non-blocking check, not an approval: approval stays human (see revision-de-ia-como-complemento-de-la-humana).

titulo.es: Controlar el acceso a S3 solo con políticas, con las ACL desactivadas y Block Public Access activado
titulo.en: Controlling S3 access with policies only, with ACLs disabled and Block Public Access on

porque.es: Con «Bucket owner enforced» el dueño del bucket posee todos los objetos y el acceso se decide solo con políticas; Block Public Access impide hacerlo público por accidente. Es la configuración por defecto de los buckets nuevos desde abril de 2023 y AWS recomienda mantenerla.
porque.en: With "Bucket owner enforced" the bucket owner owns every object and access is decided by policies alone; Block Public Access prevents making it public by accident. It has been the default for new buckets since April 2023 and AWS recommends keeping it.

evidencia.titulo: Amazon S3 Object Ownership can now disable access control lists to simplify access management for data in S3 (What's New with AWS)
evidencia.cita: When you apply this bucket-level setting, every object in an S3 bucket is owned by the bucket owner, and ACLs are no longer used to grant permissions.

evidencia.titulo: Controlling ownership of objects and disabling ACLs for your bucket (Amazon S3 User Guide, instantánea del 08-12-2021 en awsdocs/amazon-s3-userguide)
evidencia.cita: A majority of modern use cases in Amazon S3 no longer require the use of ACLs, and we recommend that you disable ACLs except in unusual circumstances where you need to control access for each object individually

evidencia.titulo: Heads-Up: Amazon S3 Security Changes Are Coming in April of 2023 (AWS News Blog, actualización del 27-04-2023)
evidencia.cita: Amazon S3 now automatically enables S3 Block Public Access and disables S3 access control lists (ACLs) for all new S3 buckets in all AWS Regions.

evidencia.titulo: Controlling ownership of objects and disabling ACLs for your bucket (Amazon S3 User Guide)
evidencia.cita: By default, Object Ownership is set to the Bucket owner enforced setting and all ACLs are disabled.

evidencia.titulo: Creating a general purpose bucket (Amazon S3 User Guide)
evidencia.cita: By default, all four Block Public Access settings are enabled. We recommend that you keep all settings enabled, unless you know that you need to turn off one or more of them for your specific use case.

nota.es: Se pueden desactivar las ACL con «Bucket owner enforced» y la guía lo recomienda.
nota.en: ACLs can be disabled with "Bucket owner enforced" and the guide recommends it.

nota.es: Pasa a ser lo que trae por defecto todo bucket nuevo: ACL desactivadas y los cuatro ajustes de Block Public Access activados.
nota.en: It becomes the default for every new bucket: ACLs disabled and all four Block Public Access settings on.

titulo.es: Separar las evals de capacidad (miden progreso, empiezan bajas) de las de regresión (cerca del 100 %, bloquean el merge)
titulo.en: Separating capability evals (measure progress, start low) from regression evals (near 100%, block the merge)

porque.es: Una suite al 100 % vigila regresiones pero no dice nada de mejoras, y una de tareas difíciles no sirve como puerta. Anthropic (enero de 2026) recomienda evals de capacidad que empiezan con una tasa baja, para mejorar, y evals de regresión cercanas al 100 %, que avisan cuando algo se rompe; las de capacidad que ya se superan «se gradúan» a la suite de regresión.
porque.en: A suite at 100% tracks regressions but says nothing about improvement, and a suite of hard tasks is useless as a gate. Anthropic (January 2026) recommends capability evals that start at a low pass rate, to improve against, and regression evals near 100%, which flag when something breaks; capability tasks that are passed reliably “graduate” to the regression suite.

evidencia.titulo: Demystifying evals for AI agents (Anthropic Engineering)
evidencia.cita: Capability or “quality” evals ask, “What can this agent do well?” They should start at a low pass rate, targeting tasks the agent struggles with and giving teams a hill to climb.

evidencia.titulo: Demystifying evals for AI agents (Anthropic Engineering)
evidencia.cita: Regression evals ask, “Does the agent still handle all the tasks it used to?” and should have a nearly 100% pass rate.

evidencia.titulo: Demystifying evals for AI agents (Anthropic Engineering)
evidencia.cita: capability evals with high pass rates can “graduate” to become a regression suite that is run continuously to catch any drift.

evidencia.titulo: Demystifying evals for AI agents (Anthropic Engineering)
evidencia.cita: An eval at 100% tracks regressions but provides no signal for improvement.

nota.es: Anthropic distingue evals de capacidad y de regresión, recomienda ejecutar ambas y graduar a regresión las tareas de capacidad que ya se superan.
nota.en: Anthropic distinguishes capability and regression evals, recommends running both and graduating capability tasks that are reliably passed into the regression suite.

titulo.es: Abrir SSH (22) o RDP (3389) a 0.0.0.0/0 en los grupos de seguridad
titulo.en: Opening SSH (22) or RDP (3389) to 0.0.0.0/0 in security groups

porque.es: Abrir el 22 o el 3389 a 0.0.0.0/0 expone el acceso administrativo a cualquiera en Internet. En 2018 la guía de EC2 lo toleraba un rato en pruebas; desde 2022 solo dice que se autoricen IP o rangos concretos. Mejor aún, no abrir puertos (ver acceso-a-instancias-sin-puertos-entrantes).
porque.en: Opening 22 or 3389 to 0.0.0.0/0 exposes administrative access to anyone on the Internet. In 2018 the EC2 guide tolerated it briefly in testing; since 2022 it only says to authorize specific IPs or ranges. Better still, open no ports (see acceso-a-instancias-sin-puertos-entrantes).

evidencia.titulo: Authorizing Inbound Traffic for Your Linux Instances (Amazon EC2 User Guide, versión de 2018)
evidencia.cita: This is acceptable for a short time in a test environment, but it's unsafe for production environments.

evidencia.titulo: Authorize inbound traffic for your Linux instances (Amazon EC2 User Guide, instantánea del 25-05-2022 en awsdocs/amazon-ec2-user-guide)
evidencia.cita: You should authorize only a specific IP address or range of addresses to access your instance

evidencia.titulo: Change the security groups for your Amazon EC2 instance (Amazon EC2 User Guide)
evidencia.cita: If you add inbound rules for ports 22 (SSH) or 3389 (RDP), we strongly recommend that you authorize only the specific IP address or range of addresses that need access to your instances.

nota.es: La guía de EC2 avisa: inseguro en producción, aceptable solo un rato en pruebas.
nota.en: The EC2 guide warns: unsafe in production, acceptable only briefly in testing.

nota.es: La guía quita la excepción de pruebas: solo IP o rangos concretos. Fecha aproximada: el cambio aparece entre las instantáneas de awsdocs del 11-03-2022 y del 25-05-2022.
nota.en: The guide drops the testing exception: specific IPs or ranges only. Approximate date: the change appears between the awsdocs snapshots of 2022-03-11 and 2022-05-25.

porque.es: Cada plataforma tenía su SDK y su formato, y cambiar de herramienta era reinstrumentar. Langfuse acepta OpenTelemetry desde febrero de 2025, y su SDK de Python v3 (junio de 2025) y el de TypeScript v4 (agosto de 2025) se basan en él; LangSmith y Phoenix (OpenInference) también lo aceptan. porque.en: Each platform had its own SDK and format, and switching tools meant re-instrumenting. Langfuse has accepted OpenTelemetry since February 2025, and its Python SDK v3 (June 2025) and TypeScript SDK v4 (August 2025) are built on it; LangSmith and Phoenix (OpenInference) accept it too. Beware when migrating: the new SDK also captures HTTP or database spans and can raise the bill. What is current: see trazas-de-agentes-con-opentelemetry-genai.

titulo.es: Aplicar la autenticación reforzada (SCA) de PSD2 a los pagos con tarjeta en línea mediante 3-D Secure 2
titulo.en: Applying PSD2 strong customer authentication (SCA) to online card payments through 3-D Secure 2

porque.es: Desde el 14 de septiembre de 2019 los pagos electrónicos en la UE exigen dos factores y un código ligado al importe y al beneficiario (en tarjetas de comercio electrónico, la EBA dio de margen hasta el 31-12-2020). En tarjetas eso se hace con EMV 3DS (3-D Secure 2), que da una experiencia más fluida y más datos para el análisis de fraude; el RTS prevé exenciones.
porque.en: Since 14 September 2019, electronic payments in the EU require two factors and a code bound to the amount and payee (for e-commerce card payments the EBA allowed until 31-12-2020). For cards this is done with EMV 3DS (3-D Secure 2), which offers a smoother experience and more data for fraud analysis; the RTS provides for exemptions.

porque.es: Esos disparadores corren con los secretos y el token del repositorio base. Si el agente trabaja sobre el checkout del PR, lee y ejecuta lo que controla el atacante: scripts, hooks y su propia configuración (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/). Desde junio de 2026, actions/checkout v7 se niega por defecto a bajar el PR de un fork con esos disparadores, y GitHub pide que el código descargado solo se inspeccione como datos.
porque.en: Those triggers run with the base repository’s secrets and token. If the agent works on the PR checkout, it reads and runs what the attacker controls: scripts, hooks and its own configuration (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/). Since June 2026, actions/checkout v7 refuses by default to check out a fork’s PR under those triggers, and GitHub asks that the checked-out code only ever be inspected as data.

evidencia.cita: this trigger, unlike the standard `pull_request` trigger, runs workflows with elevated permissions including a `GITHUB_TOKEN` which has read/write repository permission.

should be considered part of the untrusted input surface.

titulo.es: Ejecutar un agente de IA en GitHub Actions sobre issues, PR o comentarios de cualquiera, con token de escritura o secretos a su alcance
titulo.en: Running an AI agent in GitHub Actions on anyone's issues, PRs or comments, with a write token or secrets within reach

porque.es: El texto de un issue, un PR o un commit es una vía de inyección de prompts (un comentario HTML no se ve, pero el modelo lo lee). Las acciones de Anthropic y OpenAI y el agente de GitHub solo se activan por defecto con usuarios con escritura; Google pide, con datos no confiables, privilegios mínimos y herramientas limitadas, y la acción de revisión de seguridad de Anthropic avisa de que no resiste la inyección. Es la trifecta letal aplicada al CI (ver agente-con-la-trifecta-letal); la alternativa, ver agente-de-ia-en-ci-con-token-de-solo-lectura.
porque.en: The text of an issue, a PR or a commit is a prompt-injection channel (an HTML comment is invisible, but the model reads it). Anthropic’s and OpenAI’s actions and GitHub’s agent only trigger for users with write access by default; Google asks, with untrusted data, for minimum privileges and limited tools, and Anthropic’s security-review action warns it is not hardened against injection. It is the lethal trifecta applied to CI (see agente-con-la-trifecta-letal); the alternative, see agente-de-ia-en-ci-con-token-de-solo-lectura.

titulo.es: Ejecutar un agente de IA en un runner de CI con sudo y la clave del LLM en el entorno, confiando en que «solo lectura y sin red» la protege
titulo.en: Running an AI agent on a CI runner with sudo and the LLM key in the environment, trusting "read-only and no network" to protect it

porque.es: Con sudo sin contraseña en el runner, un sistema de ficheros de solo lectura y sin red no basta: OpenAI muestra cómo se puede sacar la OPENAI_API_KEY y pide desde octubre de 2025 usar drop-sudo o un usuario sin privilegios, y ejecutar el agente como último paso del job. Anthropic limpia los secretos del entorno de los subprocesos cuando su acción se abre a usuarios sin escritura (marzo de 2026).
porque.en: With passwordless sudo on the runner, a read-only filesystem and no network are not enough: OpenAI shows how OPENAI_API_KEY can be extracted and has asked since October 2025 to use drop-sudo or an unprivileged user, and to run the agent as the last step of the job. Anthropic scrubs secrets from subprocess environments when its action is opened to users without write access (March 2026).

evidencia.cita: many expect the combination of "read-only access" and no network to be a sufficient safeguard, but this is not the case in the presence of passwordless `sudo`
Recommendation: run `openai/codex-action` as the last step in a job

titulo.en: Running the CI AI agent with a read-only token and no secrets within reach, and applying its writes in a separate, validated job

porque.es: Si el agente cae en una inyección de prompt, solo puede proponer. GitHub Agentic Workflows lo hace por defecto (token de solo lectura, escrituras por «safe outputs» validados en trabajos aparte, credenciales fuera del agente); Google pide el mínimo privilegio; Anthropic, si su acción se abre a usuarios sin escritura, usar el GITHUB_TOKEN efímero y no un token personal, que la inyección puede ir sacando. Evita el antipatrón de agente-de-ia-en-ci-activable-por-cualquiera.
porque.en: If the agent falls for a prompt injection, it can only propose. GitHub Agentic Workflows does this by default (read-only token, writes through validated “safe outputs” in separate jobs, credentials kept away from the agent); Google asks for least privilege; Anthropic, if its action is opened to users without write access, to use the ephemeral GITHUB_TOKEN rather than a personal token, which injection can gradually extract. It avoids the anti-pattern in agente-de-ia-en-ci-activable-por-cualquiera.

porque.es: Los prompts y las respuestas llevan datos personales y secretos de los usuarios, y pesan mucho. porque.en: Prompts and responses carry users’ personal data and secrets, and they are bulky. Since v1.28 (October 2024), OpenTelemetry’s GenAI conventions say they should not be captured by default, only if the application enables it; beware, since instrumentations such as OpenLLMetry still record them by default unless TRACELOOP_TRACE_CONTENT=false. It is the LLM case of datos-sensibles-en-logs-y-trazas (see that id); OpenAI’s agents SDK has its own entry (see trazas-por-defecto-del-sdk-de-agentes-de-openai-con-datos-personales).

titulo.es: Cifrar con DES o con 3DES (TDEA)
titulo.en: Encrypting with DES or 3DES (TDEA)

porque.es: DES (56 bits) se rompe por fuerza bruta desde 1998 y NIST lo retiró en 2005. 3DES tiene bloques de 64 bits: Sweet32 (2016) recupera cookies de una conexión HTTPS larga con 3DES, y OpenSSL 1.1.0 lo desactivó por defecto, igual que RC4 (ver cifrado-rc4-en-tls). NIST lo desaprobó para cifrar tras el 31 de diciembre de 2023 y TLS 1.3 ya no lo incluye; en TLS 1.0 y 1.1 era el cifrado obligatorio (ver ofrecer-tls-1-0-y-1-1). Descifrar datos viejos queda como uso heredado.
porque.en: DES (56-bit) has been brute-forceable since 1998 and NIST withdrew it in 2005. 3DES has 64-bit blocks: Sweet32 (2016) recovers cookies from a long-lived 3DES HTTPS connection, and OpenSSL 1.1.0 disabled it by default "just like RC4" (see cifrado-rc4-en-tls). NIST disallowed it for encryption after 31 December 2023 and TLS 1.3 no longer includes it; in TLS 1.0 and 1.1 it was the mandatory cipher (see ofrecer-tls-1-0-y-1-1). Decrypting old data remains as legacy use.

porque.es: AES (bloques de 128 bits, claves de 128, 192 o 256) es el estándar de NIST desde 2001, y GCM le añade autenticación: cifra y detecta manipulaciones en una sola operación. TLS 1.3 solo admite algoritmos AEAD y obliga a implementar AES-128-GCM; ChaCha20-Poly1305 es la otra opción AEAD. Sustituye a 3DES (ver cifrado-3des-o-des) y a RC4 (ver cifrado-rc4-en-tls).
porque.en: AES (128-bit blocks, 128/192/256-bit keys) has been the NIST standard since 2001, and GCM adds authentication: it encrypts and detects tampering in a single operation. TLS 1.3 only allows AEAD algorithms and mandates AES-128-GCM; ChaCha20-Poly1305 is the other AEAD option. It replaces 3DES (see cifrado-3des-o-des) and RC4 (see cifrado-rc4-en-tls).

porque.es: Frena los intentos con las contraseñas más usadas o ya filtradas. NIST lo exige desde 2017, explicando al usuario por qué se rechaza; desde 2025, además, hay que comparar la contraseña entera.
porque.en: It stops guesses with the most common or already breached passwords. NIST has required it since 2017, telling the user why it was rejected; since 2025 the whole password must also be compared.

evidencia.titulo: NIST SP 800-63B, rev. 3 (texto con las actualizaciones hasta 2020-03-02)
evidencia.cita: When processing requests to establish and change memorized secrets, verifiers SHALL compare the prospective secrets against a list that contains values known to be commonly-used, expected, or compromised.

evidencia.titulo: NIST SP 800-63B, rev. 3 (texto con las actualizaciones hasta 2020-03-02)
evidencia.cita: If the chosen secret is found in the list, the CSP or verifier SHALL advise the subscriber that they need to select a different secret, SHALL provide the reason for rejection, and SHALL require the subscriber to choose a different value.
The entire password SHALL be subject to comparison, not substrings or words that might be contained therein.

nota.es: NIST SP 800-63B lo hace obligatorio («SHALL»), con el motivo del rechazo.
nota.en: NIST SP 800-63B makes it mandatory ("SHALL"), with the reason for rejection.

nota.es: NIST SP 800-63B-4: hay que comparar la contraseña entera, no trozos.
nota.en: NIST SP 800-63B-4: the whole password must be compared, not substrings.

titulo.es: Confiar solo en las cookies SameSite como defensa contra CSRF
titulo.en: Relying only on SameSite cookies as the CSRF defence

porque.es: Chrome trata como Lax las cookies sin SameSite desde 2020 (tras una marcha atrás por la COVID-19), pero OWASP lo considera defensa en profundidad: solo basta en despliegues que cumplan todas sus condiciones.
porque.en: Chrome has treated cookies without SameSite as Lax since 2020 (after a COVID-19 rollback), but OWASP sees it as defence in depth: it is only enough for deployments that meet all its conditions.

cuando.es: la aplicación cumple todas las condiciones que enumera OWASP para que SameSite baste (entre ellas, fijar SameSite de forma explícita y verificar Origin/Referer); el Lax por defecto del navegador nunca basta
cuando.en: the app meets every condition OWASP lists for SameSite to be enough (including setting SameSite explicitly and checking Origin/Referer); the browser’s default Lax is never enough

cuando.es: en cualquier otro caso
cuando.en: in any other case

porque.es: SameSite se combina con un token CSRF o el patrón de doble envío, no lo sustituye.
porque.en: SameSite is combined with a CSRF token or the double-submit pattern, not used instead of it.

evidencia.cita: Aug 11, 2020: The target rollout population has been increased to 100% of users on Chrome Stable versions 80 and above, and the actual proportion of users with the new behavior enabled is now ramping up to 100% gradually.

evidencia.titulo: Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet (OWASP)
evidencia.cita: For any application that does not meet all of the above, `SameSite` should be treated as a defense-in-depth layer and combined with a CSRF token or a double-submit pattern rather than relied on alone.

nota.es: Chrome sube al 100 % el objetivo de SameSite=Lax por defecto (previsto para Chrome 80 en febrero y aplazado en abril por la COVID-19). Ayuda, pero no convierte a SameSite en defensa suficiente.
nota.en: Chrome raises the target for SameSite=Lax by default to 100% (planned for Chrome 80 in February, rolled back in April due to COVID-19). It helps, but does not make SameSite a sufficient defence.

titulo.es: Añadir una Content-Security-Policy estricta (nonce o hash, sin unsafe-inline) como segunda capa contra XSS
titulo.en: Adding a strict Content-Security-Policy (nonce or hash, no unsafe-inline) as a second layer against XSS

porque.es: Hace mucho más difícil explotar un XSS que se haya colado, y es lo que MDN recomienda en lugar del filtro XSS del navegador. No sustituye a codificar bien la salida: OWASP avisa de que no debe ser la única defensa y de que una política demasiado permisiva se puede esquivar.
porque.en: It makes an XSS that slipped through much harder to exploit, and it is what MDN recommends instead of the browser XSS filter. It does not replace proper output encoding: OWASP warns it must not be the only defence and that an overly permissive policy can be bypassed.

evidencia.cita: Content Security Policy Level 2 W3C Recommendation, 15 December 2016
It is recommended that you use Content-Security-Policy instead of XSS filtering.
CSP should not be relied upon as the only defensive mechanism against XSS.

nota.es: CSP Level 2 es Recomendación del W3C.
nota.en: CSP Level 2 becomes a W3C Recommendation.

titulo.es: Guardar las contraseñas con una función lenta y con sal: Argon2id (o scrypt, bcrypt, PBKDF2)
titulo.en: Storing passwords with a slow, salted function: Argon2id (or scrypt, bcrypt, PBKDF2)

porque.es: El coste por intento hace inviable el ataque masivo. OWASP las ordena: Argon2id, luego scrypt, bcrypt solo en sistemas heredados y PBKDF2 (600 000 iteraciones o más) si se exige FIPS-140.
porque.en: The per-guess cost makes mass guessing infeasible. OWASP ranks them: Argon2id, then scrypt, bcrypt only for legacy systems, and PBKDF2 (600,000+ iterations) when FIPS-140 is required.

evidencia.cita: In July 2015 we announced Argon2 as a winner

evidencia.titulo: RFC 9106 — Argon2 Memory-Hard Function for Password Hashing and Proof-of-Work Applications (IRTF, Informational)
evidencia.cita: The Argon2id variant with t=1 and 2 GiB memory is the FIRST RECOMMENDED option and is suggested as a default setting for all environments.
Use Argon2id with a minimum configuration of 19 MiB of memory, an iteration count of 2, and 1 degree of parallelism.
If FIPS-140 compliance is required, use PBKDF2 with a work factor of 600,000 or more and set with an internal hash function of HMAC-SHA-256.

nota.es: Argon2 gana la Password Hashing Competition.
nota.en: Argon2 wins the Password Hashing Competition.

nota.es: RFC 9106 publica Argon2 y recomienda la variante Argon2id por defecto.
nota.en: RFC 9106 publishes Argon2 and recommends the Argon2id variant by default.

titulo.es: Guardar las contraseñas con un hash rápido (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 a secas), con o sin sal
titulo.en: Storing passwords with a fast hash (MD5, SHA-1, plain SHA-256), salted or not

porque.es: Un hash rápido permite al atacante probar miles de millones de candidatas si roba la base de datos. NIST exige desde 2017 una función de derivación con sal y factor de coste.
porque.en: A fast hash lets an attacker try billions of guesses if they steal the database. Since 2017 NIST requires a salted key derivation function with a cost factor.

evidencia.cita: Fast hashing algorithms such as SHA‑256 are not suitable for password storage because they allow attackers to perform large numbers of guesses quickly.

evidencia.titulo: NIST SP 800-63B, rev. 3 (texto con las actualizaciones hasta 2020-03-02)
evidencia.cita: Memorized secrets SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable one-way key derivation function. Key derivation functions take a password, a salt, and a cost factor as inputs then generate a password hash.
Passwords SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable password hashing scheme. Password hashing schemes take a password, a salt, and a cost factor as inputs and generate a password hash.
Hashtype is either sha1 (default), md5 or crypt -- the algorithm used to perform a one-way hash of the password.

nota.es: Django 1.3 guarda por defecto las contraseñas con SHA-1 y sal.
nota.en: Django 1.3 stores passwords as salted SHA-1 by default.

nota.es: NIST SP 800-63B: las contraseñas, con sal y una función de derivación con factor de coste.
nota.en: NIST SP 800-63B: passwords salted and processed by a key derivation function with a cost factor.

nota.es: NIST SP 800-63B-4 lo mantiene («password hashing scheme») y pide subir el coste con el tiempo.
nota.en: NIST SP 800-63B-4 keeps it ("password hashing scheme") and asks to raise the cost over time.

titulo.es: Publicar DMARC con `p=none` y dejarlo así para siempre
titulo.en: Publishing DMARC with `p=none` and leaving it that way forever

porque.es: `p=none` pide al receptor que no haga nada con el correo que falla DMARC: sirve para recoger informes, no protege contra la suplantación del dominio. RFC 9989 (mayo de 2026, sustituye a RFC 7489) lo plantea como fase inicial para auditar, seguida de `p=quarantine` (y `p=reject` solo si los usuarios del dominio no escriben en listas de correo); Microsoft lo presenta como fase de pruebas camino de `p=reject`.
porque.en: `p=none` asks receivers to do nothing with mail that fails DMARC: it is for collecting reports and gives no protection against domain spoofing. RFC 9989 (May 2026, obsoleting RFC 7489) frames it as an initial auditing stage followed by `p=quarantine` (and `p=reject` only if the domain's users do not post to mailing lists); Microsoft presents it as a testing stage on the way to `p=reject`.

evidencia.titulo: RFC 7489 — Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC)
evidencia.cita: none:  The Domain Owner requests no specific action be taken regarding delivery of messages.

evidencia.titulo: RFC 7489 — Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC)
evidencia.cita: To enable Domain Owners to receive DMARC feedback without impacting existing mail processing, discovered policies of "p=none" SHOULD NOT modify existing mail disposition processing.

evidencia.titulo: RFC 9989 — Domain-Based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC)
evidencia.cita: The reason for starting at "p=none" is to ensure that nothing's been missed in the initial SPF and DKIM deployments.

evidencia.titulo: RFC 9989 — Domain-Based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC)
evidencia.cita: first by publishing "p=none" for at least a month, followed by publishing "p=quarantine" for an equally long period of time, and comparing the message disposition results.

evidencia.titulo: RFC 9989 — Domain-Based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC)
evidencia.cita: domains that host users who might post messages to mailing lists SHOULD NOT publish Domain Owner Assessment Policies of "p=reject".

evidencia.titulo: Set up DMARC to validate email in Microsoft 365 (Microsoft Learn)
evidencia.cita: You use this value for testing and tuning of the DMARC policy

evidencia.titulo: Set up DMARC to validate email in Microsoft 365 (Microsoft Learn)
evidencia.cita: The goal is to get to a p=reject DMARC policy for all of your custom domains and subdomains, but you need to test and verify along the way to prevent destination email systems from rejecting good mail because of unintentional DMARC failures.

nota.es: RFC 7489 define `none` como «ninguna acción específica»: existe para recibir informes sin alterar cómo se trata el correo, así que no protege contra la suplantación.
nota.en: RFC 7489 defines `none` as "no specific action": it exists to receive reports without changing how mail is handled, so it does not protect against spoofing.

nota.es: RFC 9989 (DMARCbis) sustituye a RFC 7489: empezar en `p=none` para auditar SPF y DKIM, al menos un mes, y pasar luego a `p=quarantine`; `p=reject` no para dominios cuyos usuarios escriben en listas de correo.
nota.en: RFC 9989 (DMARCbis) obsoletes RFC 7489: start at `p=none` to audit SPF and DKIM, for at least a month, then move to `p=quarantine`; `p=reject` not for domains whose users post to mailing lists.

titulo.es: No instalar versiones de dependencias publicadas hace menos de unos días (minimumReleaseAge, --uploaded-prior-to)
titulo.en: Not installing dependency versions published less than a few days ago (minimumReleaseAge, --uploaded-prior-to)

porque.es: Las versiones maliciosas de paquetes populares se suelen detectar y retirar enseguida (pnpm habla de menos de una hora); esperar un margen evita instalarlas. pnpm lo añadió en la 10.16 (septiembre de 2025), npm en la 11.10 (febrero de 2026, min-release-age) y pip acepta un plazo en días desde la 26.1 (abril de 2026).
porque.en: Malicious versions of popular packages are usually detected and pulled quickly (pnpm says within an hour); waiting a margin avoids installing them. pnpm added it in 10.16 (September 2025), npm in 11.10 (February 2026, min-release-age) and pip accepts a duration in days since 26.1 (April 2026).

evidencia.cita: In most cases, such attacks are discovered quickly and the malicious versions are removed from the registry within an hour.
Add ``--uploaded-prior-to`` option to only consider packages uploaded prior to a given datetime
Allow ``--uploaded-prior-to`` to accept a duration in days (e.g., ``P3D`` for 3 days ago).
add min-release-age

nota.en: pnpm 10.16 adds minimumReleaseAge after several attacks on popular packages.

nota.en: pip 26.0 adds --uploaded-prior-to.

nota.en: npm 11.10.0 adds the min-release-age option.

nota.en: pip 26.1 accepts the margin in days.

titulo.es: Instalar paquetes privados de Python con «pip install --extra-index-url» apuntando al índice interno
titulo.en: Installing private Python packages with "pip install --extra-index-url" pointing at the internal index

porque.es: pip mezcla las versiones de todos los índices, así que cualquiera puede subir a PyPI un paquete con el nombre del interno y que se instale el suyo (torchtriton en PyTorch-nightly, diciembre de 2022). pip lo advierte desde la 21.1 (abril de 2021); uv solo mira más allá del primer índice que tenga el paquete si se le pide expresamente.
porque.en: pip merges versions from every index, so anyone can upload a package with the internal name to PyPI and get theirs installed (torchtriton in PyTorch-nightly, December 2022). pip has warned about it since 21.1 (April 2021); uv only looks past the first index that has the package if explicitly asked.

evidencia.cita: Add warning about ``--extra-index-url`` and dependency confusion
Using the ``--extra-index-url`` option to search for packages which are not in the main repository (for example, private packages) is unsafe.
Allow package lookups across multiple indexes via explicit opt-in

evidencia.titulo: uv — Compatibility with pip: packages that exist on multiple indexes
evidencia.cita: The intent is to prevent "dependency confusion" attacks, in which an attacker publishes a malicious package on PyPI with the same name as an internal package

evidencia.titulo: PyTorch — Compromised PyTorch-nightly dependency chain between December 25th and December 30th, 2022
evidencia.cita: Since the PyPI index takes precedence, this malicious package was being installed instead of the version from our official repository.

nota.es: pip 21.1 añade a la documentación el aviso de que --extra-index-url para paquetes privados es inseguro.
nota.en: pip 21.1 adds the docs warning that --extra-index-url for private packages is unsafe.

nota.es: PyTorch informa de que torchtriton malicioso en PyPI se instaló en lugar del de su índice nightly entre el 25 y el 30 de diciembre de 2022.
nota.en: PyTorch reports that a malicious torchtriton on PyPI was installed instead of the one from its nightly index between 25 and 30 December 2022.

nota.es: uv 0.1.29 deja la búsqueda en varios índices como opción explícita («unsafe-any-match»); por defecto se queda con el primer índice que tiene el paquete para evitar la confusión de dependencias.
nota.en: uv 0.1.29 makes multi-index lookup an explicit opt-in (`unsafe-any-match`); by default it sticks to the first index that has the package to prevent dependency confusion.

titulo.es: Dar acceso a la nube a las personas con federación (SSO) y credenciales temporales
titulo.en: Giving people cloud access through federation (SSO) and temporary credentials

porque.es: Las credenciales temporales caducan solas y las altas y bajas de personas se hacen en un único proveedor de identidad. Es la primera buena práctica de la guía de IAM de AWS desde su reescritura de 2022, que recomienda IAM Identity Center. Para las cargas de trabajo y el CI, lo mismo con roles y OIDC (ver oidc-para-credenciales-en-ci).
porque.en: Temporary credentials expire on their own, and people are added and removed in a single identity provider. It has been the first best practice in AWS's IAM guide since its 2022 rewrite, which recommends IAM Identity Center. For workloads and CI, the same with roles and OIDC (see oidc-para-credenciales-en-ci).

evidencia.titulo: Security best practices in IAM (AWS IAM User Guide, instantánea del 18-07-2022 en awsdocs/iam-user-guide)
evidencia.cita: Require your human users to use temporary credentials when accessing AWS

evidencia.titulo: Security best practices in IAM (AWS IAM User Guide)
evidencia.cita: For centralized access management, we recommend that you use AWS IAM Identity Center (IAM Identity Center) to manage access to your accounts and permissions within those accounts.

nota.es: Primera buena práctica de IAM: personas federadas con un proveedor de identidad y credenciales temporales; AWS recomienda IAM Identity Center (antes AWS SSO). Fecha aproximada: aparece entre las instantáneas de awsdocs del 16-11-2021 y del 18-07-2022.
nota.en: First IAM best practice: people federated through an identity provider with temporary credentials; AWS recommends IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO). Approximate date: it appears between the awsdocs snapshots of 2021-11-16 and 2022-07-18.
